| 0 | full | `X` | `INPUT_RANGE_STRAFE_LEFT_RIGHT` | "would translate X instead of turning" |
| 1 | full | `Y` | `INPUT_RANGE_STRAFE_UP_DOWN` | "...and Y" |
| 2 | full | `Z` | `INPUT_RANGE_THROTTLE` | "throttle reversed" |
| 3 | **partial** | `RX` | `INPUT_RANGE_STEERING_PRIMARY` | (the mini-stick; barely touched) |
| 4 | **partial** | `RY` | `INPUT_RANGE_STEERING_PITCH` | (ditto) |
| 5 | full | `RZ` | **`INPUT_STATE_FIRE_PRIMARY_WEAPON`** | "the rudder twist fired shot" |

**Four independent behaviours, one explanation.** Strafing on the stick,
throttle on the throttle, firing on the twist, and steering barely responding
are four *different* bindings with four *different* observable effects, and
all four line up with SDL axis index = conventional evdev order
(`ABS_X`=0 … `ABS_RZ`=5). That is corroboration from genuinely independent
sources, not four copies of one cause.

**Steering was never dead. It is on axes 3/4 — the mini-stick on the
throttle** — which the sweep only moved partially (`3:-9638..8609`,
`4:-3470..385` against a ±32768 range). "Plugged it in and it didn't work"
was a thumb-stick nobody thought to use.

`invert_throttle` is already a `<param>` in the inputmap's `<config>` block,
sitting at `false`.

### The fix, and the decision that is NOT mine

A rebind: steering onto 0/1, strafe onto 3/4, drop the `RZ` fire binding
(twisting a stick should not shoot), flip `invert_throttle`. It would ship
non-intrusively through the inputmap rewrite that already moves `MOUSELOOK`
to F13 — the player changes nothing.

**Whether X4VRMOD should ship a device-specific profile at all is Patola's
call**, not a technical question. X4 also has its own per-device profiles
(`inputmap_1..5.xml`), which may be the right mechanism rather than ours.
Nothing is being built until he says which.

### Instrument defect fixed in the same pass

The `pad axes` ranges are cumulative, so every periodic report restated the
whole history and take 309 printed **130 near-identical lines** — a wall that
buries the one line anyone reads. The block now prints the **last** line per
family, plus which axes were swept to their stops and which were not, because
"this axis did not move" read off a partial sweep is the same error as
reporting zero for an input nobody supplied.

### #46 is still unmeasured

`pointer x=335..1408 y=83..1408` — 38% x 47%, and `1408` is the mouse-look
park again. The corner sweep did not happen (Patola got caught in a menu he
had opened by accident), so this is another run that says where the pointer
went, not where it can go. **The reachability protocol is still owed.**

## #71 CLOSED — controllers work; the binding fix is a SHIP-TIME decision

Patola's call after take 309, recorded verbatim in substance: he does not plan
to play X4 with the X52, so fixing its bindings now is not work worth doing.
What matters is that **a player who chooses that control scheme can use it
seamlessly** — a shipping concern, not an investigation. His own preference is
his sc-controller scheme emulating **mouse and keyboard**.

So:

* **The controller question is answered and closed.** Analog pad steering
  works under head-look (take 307); the X52 enumerates, opens, and delivers
  all nine axes (take 309); every symptom is a default binding, with steering
  sitting on the throttle's mini-stick.
* **The HOTAS becomes a REGRESSION CHECK**, run after the mouse-shim work
  lands, to verify the shim has not disabled controllers. Not a lead, not a
  blocker, and not scheduled before then.
* **No device-specific profile is being built.** If one ships later, X4's own
  per-device profiles (`inputmap_1..5.xml`) are a candidate mechanism
  alongside our inputmap rewrite.

### What this does to the shim's priorities

His preferred input is emulated **mouse and keyboard**, and two things are now
measured about that combination:

* **Mouse steering cannot work while head-look holds MOUSELOOK**, and that is
  X4's own structure, not ours — our `xrel`/`yrel` drop is a second cause on
  top of it. This applies to ANY mouse source, including sc-controller's
  emulated one.
* **Arrow keys steer fine** under head-look, and so does an analog pad axis.

So for his scheme the shim's job is **the cursor — aiming, menus, HUD clicks —
and not steering**. That makes **#46 the highest-value remaining shim item**,
ahead of #64 and #72, because it is what he actually touches every session.

A note for his own toolchain, not for this repo: sc-controller can emit a
gamepad axis as well as mouse motion, and take 307 proved an analog axis
steers under head-look while mouse motion cannot. A touchpad mapped to the
emulated pad's right stick would reach `INPUT_RANGE_STEERING_PRIMARY`/`PITCH`
and give analog steering that survives head-look — with nothing required from
this mod. His software, his call; recorded because the measurement that makes
it worth trying is ours.

### #46's protocol, still owed

Three runs have now reported where the pointer WENT rather than where it can
go, with `x` capped at 1408 — the mouse-look park — in two of them. The
measurement needs a take whose protocol deliberately drives the pointer into
all four corners with a cursor on screen (map or menu open). It rides any
take; it does not need one of its own.

## #46 — the mechanism, derived from measured numbers with no take spent

### The cursor is confined to the central 52.5% of the eye, by the canvas

Both take 307 and take 309 log the live affine as **`A=(0.5252,0.5252)`,
`B=(+0.00002,+0.00000)`**. The draw applies it to the hotspot
(`layer/x4vr_cursor_draw.hpp`), so for a pointer anywhere in `[0, eye]`:

    drawn = 0.5252 * (2*px/eye - 1) + 0.00002   in [-0.5252, +0.5252]

    pointer at the left/top edge   -> drawn at   668.5 px
    pointer at the centre          -> drawn at  1408.0 px
    pointer at the right/bottom    -> drawn at  2147.5 px

**A 1479x1479 box centred in the 2816x2816 eye. A 669 px border on every side
where no cursor can ever appear, and 72.4% of the eye's AREA unreachable** —
whatever the player does with the mouse.

That is "invisible over much of the eye image", it is arithmetic rather than a
hypothesis, and it cost no run.

### Why three takes could not see it

The census measured the **published pointer range**, which is a fact about the
protocol — where Patola happened to move the mouse — not about the geometry.
Take 307 read 67%x72%, take 308 read a flat 1408 (X4 parks the pointer at the
window centre for mouse-look), take 309 read 38%x47% after he got stuck in a
menu. Three different numbers for a quantity that never changed.

**The instrument measured a proxy for the thing.** Now it measures the thing:
`cursor drawn (...)` reports the min/max of the **mapped** hotspot in NDC and
as a percentage of the eye, so it is independent of how far the mouse was
moved. [[instrument-inherits-its-question]].

### This is the UI canvas working as designed — and that is the question

The cursor takes the same map as the UI on purpose: X4 hit-tests CPU-side at
an unshifted window coordinate, so if the menu moves and the pointer does not,
every button still *works* while the pointer sits away from it. For **menus**
the confinement is correct — the UI is there too.

**It is wrong for anything outside the canvas.** A defect report of "the
cursor is invisible over much of the eye" is a report that the player wanted
to point at something the canvas does not cover.

**Whether the cursor should be confined to the UI canvas is a design decision
and it is Patola's**, not a defect to be silently fixed. The options differ in
what they break, and none is obviously right:

1. leave it — correct for menus, useless for anything in the periphery;
2. unmap the cursor (draw at the raw pointer position) — reaches the whole eye
   and immediately separates from every button it activates, which is the
   exact failure the map was added to prevent;
3. map the cursor only while a menu/map is up and leave it unmapped otherwise
   — needs a reliable "is the UI capturing the pointer" predicate, and #72
   already shows our view-state predicates are not always right;
4. widen the canvas itself (#86 is already about per-context canvas distance).

### An ambiguity I could not settle, and did not guess

Two processes in the tree report different window sizes —
`5632x2816` from the pid the layer runs in, `2816x2816` from another — and
from the layer's side I cannot tell which one feeds the pointer. It matters:
if the input path is in a 5632-wide space while the eye is 2816, the pointer
and the image are in different coordinate systems and every placement number
is measured across that seam.

So the census now publishes `shared->window_w` — **the width the injector
published next to the position it published** — on the same line as the eye
extent, and the scorer prints `THE INPUT PATH AND THE IMAGE DISAGREE` and
**suppresses the confinement verdict** when they differ. A seam outranks a
geometry reading taken across it.

### Instruments

* `cursor drawn (...)` — mapped-hotspot NDC extent, percentage of eye, and the
  channel's window width. Verified on the GPU harness (`cursor_render`, 0
  validation errors) before any take, per [[x4vr-headless-gpu-harness]].
* `tests/run-census-scorer.sh` gained 9 cases: the measured 0.5252 confinement
  with its border and lost-area figures, an unconfined **negative control** so
  the verdict is a discriminator and not an off switch, and the seam case with
  a check that confinement is NOT reported across it.

## #86 read, and it does NOT fold into #46 — option 4 is a regression

### They are different terms of the same matrix, and the code says so

`make_canvas_k()` in `common/x4vr_view.hpp`:

    k[0] = k[5] = ui_half_tan * |sx_screen|     <- the SCALE   (#81, #46's cause)
    k[12] -= ax_num * d_eye / z                 <- the DISPARITY (#86's subject)

with its own comment: *"NOT applied to k[12]. That is the canvas DISPARITY,
set by the canvas distance z, and a plane's disparity does not depend on where
content sits within the plane."*

**#86 is about how far away the canvas appears. #46 is about how much of the
field it covers.** Independent terms. Doing #86 would not touch #46's number
and doing #46 would not touch #86's.

### And the scale is #81, which means option 4 regresses #76

`0.5252 / 0.75 = 0.7003`, and `ui_half_tan` is **0.75** — the tangent of the
36.87 deg half-angle **X4 lays its UI out against**, whatever `<fov>` we set
(#45, measured in take 261). The scale is what puts a UI element at the ANGLE
X4 meant. Remove or widen it and the UI is displayed
`tan(half_world)/0.75 = 1.904x` too far out, which **is #76's sliding HUD** —
a closed task, default ON since take 268.

So *"widen the canvas"* is not a tweak with a cost; it is undoing a correct
fix. **Option 4 is withdrawn.**

### Which raises a harder question: is #46 a defect at all?

The UI and the cursor take the **same** map. X4 hit-tests CPU-side in its own
unshifted space, and both the button and the pointer are scaled by the same
0.5252, so they agree. The cursor is confined to exactly the region the UI
occupies — and **there is nothing outside it to point at**, because X4 never
drew UI there.

Further, while head-look holds MOUSELOOK, X4 suspends mouse control entirely
(#71), so there is no mouse aiming at world objects to be denied.

### The original symptom does not follow from the current code

*"Cursor is invisible over much of the eye image **until moved down**"* is a
**vertical asymmetry**. The measured map is symmetric — `k[0] == k[5]`, and
take 309 logs `B=(+0.00002,+0.00000)`, so `by` is zero and there is no
vertical shift at all. Nothing in the present arithmetic can make the cursor
behave differently up versus down.

**So #46's report either predates this code or is about something the
confinement does not explain.** [[stale-comment-is-misinformation]] — and
building a fix for a symptom that may no longer reproduce is how this project
has spent takes before.

### Recommendation: do not choose between 3 and 4 yet

Option 4 is dead. Option 3 (map the cursor only while the UI is capturing the
pointer) is viable but needs a predicate, and #72 is standing evidence that
our view-state predicates are not always right — so it is real work, to be
spent only on a symptom that reproduces.

What is missing is one observation, and it is Patola's eye rather than a
measurement: **with the cursor visible, is it still wrong, and where?** The
`cursor drawn` instrument now reports the confinement as a number on any take,
so the question to him is only "does the confined region match what you see,
and does anything you need to point at fall outside it".

## P310 — committed before the run: is #46's confinement what Patola sees?

Take 309's line, new name and log. No knob changes. **Runtime WiVRn**
(`XR_RUNTIME_JSON` unset).

**Controller configuration: NO emulated pad — real mouse and keyboard.** The
pad is irrelevant to #46 and would actively confound it, because his inputmap
binds `INPUT_JOYAXIS_RX/RY` to **four** things at once:

    INPUT_RANGE_STEERING_PRIMARY        (flight)
    INPUT_RANGE_CONTROLLERMOUSECURSOR_X (menus)
    INPUT_RANGE_MAP_ROTATE_LEFT_RIGHT   (map)
    INPUT_RANGE_FP_YAW                  (on foot)

So the right touchpad he has just mapped to the emulated right stick would,
**in a menu, drive X4's own controller cursor** — a second cursor path that
does not go through `SDL_GetMouseState` and therefore never reaches
`publish_cursor`. The overlay would keep drawing the stale SDL pointer while
X4 moved a different cursor on screen. That is worth knowing about on its own,
and it is not what this take is for.

* **P310.1** `cursor drawn` reports about **53%x53%** of the eye, matching
  `0.75 * 0.7003`. The instrument has never run; this is its first reading and
  a known answer is the right thing to check it against.
* **P310.2** the channel's `window_w` **equals** the eye width, so no
  `THE INPUT PATH AND THE IMAGE DISAGREE`. If it disagrees, that seam outranks
  everything else here and the confinement number is void.
* **P310.3 — the falsifier that matters.** The cursor stops **symmetrically**:
  the same distance from the edge going up as going down. `k[0] == k[5]` and
  `by = 0.00000`, so nothing in the current arithmetic can do otherwise.
  **If Patola sees it reach further down than up, the canvas is NOT #46's
  cause and there is a second mechanism** — and that, not the confinement, is
  what the remaining work would be about.

## Take 310 — #46's original report does NOT reproduce, and a worse defect does

### P310.1 and P310.2 HELD; the confinement is real and CORRECT in the map

    cursor  DRAWN over ndc x=-0.5252..0.5248 y=-0.5252..0.5248 = 52%x52%
    cursor  pointer x=0..2815 y=0..2815  (100% of the window — swept properly)

No `DISAGREE`, so `window_w == eye`: **no coordinate seam**. And the pointer
covered the whole window while the drawn cursor covered 52%, which is exactly
what separating the two instruments was for.

**P310.3 is moot and that is the answer.** Patola: *"I opened the map and the
cursor would go through the entire quad corners, it would not stop midway. It
correctly selected the elements on the map as I would click them... there is no
question if it was symmetric — it was perfectly fitted to the map."*

The cursor reaches the corners of the **UI canvas**, which is the 52% region.
It matches the UI because it takes the UI's map. **#46 as written — "invisible
over much of the eye image until moved down" — does not reproduce, and the
confinement is correct behaviour wherever X4's screen-space UI is what you are
pointing at.**

### The cockpit, which is a different and much worse defect

Patola: *"the cursor didn't seem consistent. I would not guess when I would be
able to click something, and I had to do several clicks to select an element...
There were some times that even with the head centered clicking on 1/4 of
screen distant from an element would select it... **There was never a cursor
change when hovering something.**"*

The last sentence is the diagnostic. X4 changes cursor on hover; that is X4's
own statement about where it thinks the pointer is, and **it never fired**.

The arithmetic accounts for all of it. The cursor is drawn at `A*n` with
`A = 0.5252`; X4 hit-tests at the raw `n`; a cockpit target **appears** at `n`:

| target at ndc | pointer needed to put the SEEN cursor on it | |
|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 0.48 | |
| 0.50 | 0.95 | |
| 0.75 | **1.43** | off the window |
| 1.00 | **1.90** | off the window |

So beyond `n = 0.525` the required pointer position **does not exist**, and
hover can never register — *"there was never a cursor change"*. And read the
other way, a click that DOES select lands with the cursor drawn `0.4748*n`
away: 6% of the eye width at `n=0.25`, 12% at `n=0.5`, **24% at the edge** —
*"clicking on 1/4 of screen distant from an element would select it"*.

**The cursor follows the UI canvas, and cockpit targets are not on it.** That
is the defect, it is well defined, and it makes the game hard to play — which
#46's original wording never conveyed.

### Which settles the option 3 vs 4 question

Option 4 was already withdrawn (it regresses #76). **Option 3 is now measured
rather than supposed**, and the predicate is not "is a menu up" in the abstract
— it is *"is the thing under the pointer on the canvas, or in the world"*.

### The A/B, and it is an elimination not a fix

New knob **`X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS`, default 1 = every prior take's behaviour**, so
no state changes. Setting it 0 passes `nullptr` for the canvas and draws the
cursor at the raw pointer position.

**Prediction: it inverts both halves.** Cockpit clicking becomes predictable
and hover starts working; the map/menus break, with the cursor offset from the
buttons it activates. If both flip, the mechanism is settled and the fix is
per-context. If the cockpit does NOT improve, the canvas is not the cause and
this whole account is wrong — which is the point of running it.

See [[x4vr-eliminate-dont-instrument]]: switch the candidate off and
re-measure, rather than building a probe to watch it.

## P311 — the cursor-canvas A/B, alternating within one run

`X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS_AB=30` alternates every 30 s, **phase 0 = ARM A = canvas
ON = the shipped default**, so a run that dies early dies in the known state.
Transitions are logged by the code that takes the branch, and the census keeps
the drawn extent **per arm** so the log can prove the knob acted before any of
Patola's report is read.

**Controller configuration: no emulated pad, real mouse and keyboard** — same
reason as take 310: `INPUT_JOYAXIS_RX/RY` drives `CONTROLLERMOUSECURSOR` in
menus, a second cursor path we do not instrument.

**Runtime: WiVRn.**

### What each arm should do

| | ARM A — canvas ON (current) | ARM B — canvas OFF |
|---|---|---|
| **map / menus** | cursor sits ON the buttons, clicking works — take 310 confirmed this | cursor drifts OFF the buttons, the error **growing toward the edge** and near zero at the centre |
| **cockpit** | hover never highlights; selection unpredictable; clicks land ~1/4 screen away at the edge — take 310 | hover should start highlighting; selection should become predictable |
| **reach** | 52% of the eye | 100% of the eye |

* **P311.1** The census reports **ARM A ~52%, ARM B ~100%**, and the scorer
  prints `THE KNOB ACTED`. If it prints `THE KNOB DID NOT ACT`, nothing else in
  this run is scorable and my whole account of #46 is wrong.
* **P311.2** **Hover highlighting appears in the cockpit during ARM B and
  never during ARM A.** This is the sharpest observable: take 310 reported
  *"there was never a cursor change when hovering something"* across the whole
  run, so any hover at all is a change of state.
* **P311.3** The map INVERTS — correct in A, wrong in B. **Both halves must
  flip.** If the cockpit improves and the map does not break, the canvas map
  is not the whole mechanism and something else is displacing the cursor.

### What would refute this

A run where the cockpit does not improve in ARM B. The account says the cursor
is drawn at `A*n` while X4 hit-tests at `n`; drawing at `n` must therefore put
the cursor where X4 tests. If it does not, the displacement is somewhere else
and the arithmetic above is a coincidence.

## Take 311 — the map half is SETTLED; P311.2 is REFUTED and the cockpit is not the canvas

    cursor  A/B ran 17 phase(s): ARM A x9, ARM B x8
    cursor  ARM A (canvas ON):  drawn over 50%x37% of the eye, 8543 frame(s)
    cursor  ARM B (canvas OFF): drawn over 100%x67% of the eye, 7185 frame(s)
    cursor  => THE KNOB ACTED.

### SETTLED: the canvas map is right for the map, and ARM A stays the default

**P311.1 HELD** — the knob acted, 50% against 100%.

**P311.3 HELD, both halves.** Patola: *"the cursor changed the reach between
the two modes, being halfway at one time (matching the map) and going to all
the reach in another"*; *"In the half-reach mode, the map works and in the
full-reach mode, it had the error you mentioned"*; and *"In the map, the error
seems to grow with distance from the centre."*

That is the full predicted inversion including its gradient. **The canvas map
is correct for X4's screen-space UI, `X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS` stays at 1, and #46's
original report is closed as not-reproducing.**

### REFUTED: P311.2, and the reason is a mistake in how I read a null

*"In the cockpit, in whatever mode I was, I couldn't get the cursor to change,
so hovering had no effect."* Hover fails in **both** arms. Bypassing the canvas
did not fix cockpit hover and did not make selection predictable — *"I could
click on some elements in each mode but couldn't see a clear pattern."*

And the sentence that explains why the prediction was bad in the first place:

> *"It would only change when I got to the map and did something — like
> clicking on an element (to become an arrow), or clicking away from an element
> (where it becomes a cross...)"*

**X4 changes the cursor in the MAP, on CLICK. Not on hover, and not in the
cockpit at all.** So take 310's *"there was never a cursor change when hovering
something"* was never evidence about where X4 thought the pointer was — **the
signal whose absence I read does not exist in that context.** I used a null
without establishing that the observable exists there, which needed one
positive control and got none.

The arithmetic that explained the map so exactly explained nothing about the
cockpit. It was not wrong; it was answering a different question.

### So what IS the cockpit defect? Unknown, and NOT to be guessed at

Candidates exist — #84's constant bracket offset, X4 hit-testing world targets
against its own UI field, the cursor's zero disparity against finite-depth
ships, head-look moving the world under a window-space pointer — and naming
four is exactly the position that has cost this project takes before
([[three-fixes-one-unmeasured-number]]).

**The next step is a control, not a hypothesis: run VANILLA X4, flatscreen, no
mod, and find out whether cockpit click-to-select is reliable there at all.**
[[x4vr-establish-which-side-is-correct]] — run the unmodified program before
deciding which side is the defect, the same move that settled #50. It costs no
VR take and no headset time.

* if vanilla is **also** unreliable and hover also never fires -> it is X4's
  own behaviour, #46's cockpit half is not ours, and the honest answer to a
  player is a control-scheme recommendation;
* if vanilla is **reliable** -> it is ours, and the vanilla run also gives the
  reference behaviour to compare against.

### Instrument defects fixed in this pass

* The single-arm `CONFINED` verdict fired off `cd[-1]` — whichever arm logged
  last — and printed *"can only ever occupy 100%x67% ... a border of about
  0%"*, a statement about neither arm. Now suppressed when both arms are
  present, because the per-arm lines ARE the result.
* **My first attempt at that suppression set `fx = fy = -1`** and the
  `fx < 90` branch duly reported *"-1%x-1% ... 100% of the AREA
  unreachable"*. Gated on a flag now.
  [[verdict-that-fires-whatever-the-number-is]] — interpretation belongs inside
  a branch on the number, and **a sentinel is not a branch**.

### Protocol feedback worth keeping

*"I lost count of how many times it switched. It's rough to give attention to
one aspect while focusing on the other aspects."* The handover asked for four
simultaneous observations during a manual task. **One primary observable per
take, and the rest only if they are free.** The phase count was not free — it
was a second task — and the log already had it.

## VANILLA CONTROL — does X4's cockpit cursor feedback exist at all?

**Not a take.** No injector, no layer, no VR, no headset, no `X4VR_LOG`, and
therefore **nothing for `score_run.py` to read** — stated explicitly because
every *take* in this project gets the scorer as its acceptance check, and this
run cannot ([[x4vr-hand-off-with-the-scorer]] does not apply where there is no
log).

The control is clean: the layer is activated **explicitly** by our launcher via
`VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH` + `VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS`, there is **no implicit layer
manifest installed**, and the injector arrives only by `LD_PRELOAD` from the
same script. Launching X4 any other way picks up neither.

### The one question

**Does X4 EVER change the cursor when the pointer is over a clickable cockpit
target?**

This is the positive control that take 311 showed was missing. Take 310's
*"there was never a cursor change when hovering something"* was read as X4
telling us where it thought the pointer was — but X4 changes the cursor **in
the map, on click**, and possibly nowhere else, in which case that silence
carried no information and the account built on it was void.

**It is fov-independent**: either the feature exists in the cockpit or it does
not.

### Free, from the same act of looking

Is cockpit click-to-select **reliable** in vanilla?

### What this does NOT answer, stated so a clean result is not over-read

His `config.xml` has **`<fov>1.1111</fov>` at 3400x1440**; our served profile
uses **1.4917 at 2816x2816**. So vanilla differs from our runs in **fov AND
resolution**, which is two variables. Per #45 the UI is laid out at X4's
default field whatever `<fov>` says, so vanilla already carries some
UI-vs-world mismatch — smaller than ours, not zero.

**"Vanilla clicks fine" therefore does NOT prove the wide field is harmless.**
It would only mean X4's cockpit clicking works somewhere, which is the
reference the next step needs.

### Protect his config first

Vanilla X4 writes `config.xml`. Ours never does — it forks
`config-x4vrmod.xml` and redirects every write into it, precisely because X4
saves settings while running; the header records the incident that forced it,
*"a config.xml left at 2816x1408 / antialiasing=none afterwards"*. A vanilla
run at his desktop resolution will rewrite his own file, so it gets copied
aside first. Same rule as [[failed-run-overwrote-data]], one directory over.

### How it reads

* **cursor never changes over a cockpit target, and selection is unreliable**
  -> X4's own behaviour. #46's cockpit half is **not ours**, and the honest
  answer to a player is a control-scheme recommendation rather than a fix.
* **cursor never changes, but selection IS reliable** -> the feature does not
  exist and my hover premise was void, but the unreliability is still ours.
  The next step measures WHERE the click lands, not whether it highlights.
* **cursor DOES change over targets** -> the feature exists, its absence in
  takes 310/311 was real evidence after all, and the account deserves another
  look at the wide field specifically.

## VANILLA CONTROL — ANSWERED: the hover signal EXISTS, and take 311's lesson inverts

Patola ran unmodified X4, flatscreen, from Steam. **It changed nothing in his
config or inputmap**, so the backup was unnecessary and the precaution cost
nothing.

**X4's cockpit hover feedback is unmissable:**

* **arrow** when the pointer is NOT over a clickable element;
* **cross inside a circle** when it IS — ships, stations, gates, even asteroids
  when close;
* **equally at any part of the screen, centre or edges.**

And a correction he made to his own report, which matters: the element's white
4-corner contour appears when it is **CLICKED**, not hovered, and disappears on
deselect. **So the cursor SHAPE is the only hover observable there is.**

### What this does to take 311's conclusion

Take 310's *"there was never a cursor change when hovering something"* **was
real evidence after all.** X4 does this feature, everywhere on screen, and in
our runs it never fired.

Take 311 refuted the *prediction* (bypass the canvas -> hover returns). On one
passing remark — that X4 changes the cursor in the map on click — I concluded
the signal did not exist in the cockpit and **discarded the observation**. That
was wrong, and the control I had already decided to run is what caught it.

**A failed prediction refutes the weakest LINK in the chain, not the
observation at the end of it.** What died was "the canvas displacement is why
hover never fires", not "hover never fires". See
[[state-the-instrument-range]], which now carries the corrected version.

### So the state of #46's cockpit half

**X4 never registers the pointer over a cockpit target under our mod, in either
cursor-canvas arm.** That is the defect. The canvas map is not the cause — ARM
B put the drawn cursor at the raw pointer and hover still never fired.

### The gap, and the instrument that closes it

`SDL_SetCursor` was hooked and **counted nothing**, so no stored log can say
whether X4 ever switched cursor during cockpit flight. Takes 310 and 311 show
26 cursor *creations* with 10 distinct hotspots and nothing about which was
*set* when.

X4 imports only `SDL_CreateColorCursor` and `SDL_SetCursor` (`nm -D`), both
hooked, so a set whose handle we cannot find is a defect and not a missing
hook. The new `cursor sets:` line separates the three cases, which want
different work:

    sets = 0            X4 never registered a hover. The pointer never landed
                        on a target -> the question is placement.
    sets > 0, found = 0 X4 changed the cursor and we kept compositing the old
                        image. OURS, invisible, and a stale composite.
    sets > 0, found > 0 X4 changed it and we published the right image, so the
                        shape DID change on screen and something else is wrong.

`changed` counts only sets that differ from the previous cursor, because X4
re-asserts the same one in some states and counting those would report a hover
on every frame of a run that never had one.

It rides the next take of any kind. **No dedicated run.**

## P312 — which of three? The cursor-set census, first reading

Take 311's line **minus** `X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS_AB`: the canvas stays at its
default ON, which take 311 settled is correct for X4's screen-space UI. One
variable, and the primary observable is the **log**, not Patola's eye — the
vanilla control already supplied the eye half.

**Controller configuration: no emulated pad, real mouse and keyboard.**
**Runtime: WiVRn.**

* **P312.1** `cursor sets` prints. It cannot be absent unless the build is
  stale: the zero case is printed explicitly, gated only on X4 having built a
  cursor at all.
* **P312.2** `changed <= 1`, i.e. **X4 never changes the cursor**, matching
  takes 310 and 311 and the report that hover never fires. This is the
  prediction; the interesting outcomes are the other two.
* **P312.3** `NOT found = 0`. X4 imports only `SDL_CreateColorCursor` and
  `SDL_SetCursor`, both hooked, so every handle it sets should be one we
  captured. A non-zero `NOT found` means we composited a stale image and the
  shape question was never answerable from the screen — which would be ours,
  and would supersede P312.2 rather than sit beside it.

### What each outcome sends us to next

* **`changed <= 1`** -> X4 is hit-testing a position the pointer never reaches.
  The canvas is exonerated (take 311's ARM B drew at the raw pointer), so the
  next question is what position X4 tests against — and #84's constant bracket
  offset becomes the lead rather than a bystander.
* **`NOT found > 0`** -> our capture missed a cursor. Ours, cheap, and it must
  be fixed before any placement work, because until then nobody can see what X4
  is doing with the shape.
* **`changed > 1` with `NOT found = 0`** -> hover DID register and the shape DID
  change on screen. That contradicts two takes and the earlier reading was of
  something else entirely; the honest next step would be to ask Patola to look
  again with that knowledge.

## Releasing head-look: nothing exists, and the design makes the state unreachable

Asked what exists for releasing head-look on demand. **Nothing player-facing**,
and the reason is structural rather than an omission.

The key is held **level-triggered** — `send_key_down` every 32nd pose while
`may_steer`, and released for as long as `!may_steer` (take 147 proved an
edge-triggered release cannot correct a re-entry it did not observe). The three
release paths:

| release | and then |
|---|---|
| `head_share_read` fails — no pose | VR tracking is dead anyway |
| `stale > 5000` — layer stopped publishing | same |
| `!may_steer`, i.e. `!(cockpit && hud)` | **X4's targeting brackets ARE the HUD** |

`may_steer = cockpit && hud` is **exactly** the condition for holding the key.
So *cockpit + HUD up + MOUSELOOK not held* cannot occur: every release path
either kills tracking or removes the things we want to hover. The two halves of
the test are mutually exclusive **by construction**, which is why no knob for
it exists.

### What does reach it: `X4VR_HEADLOOK=0`, an existing knob

`headlook_tick()` returns before anything is forced, and `headlook_enabled()`
also gates the inputmap rewrite — so `INPUT_STATE_CAMERA_MOUSELOOK` stays on
X4's own binding and nothing of ours touches it. Stereo, SBS, the layer and the
cursor overlay are unaffected. The cost is that the view will not follow his
head for the run, which is uncomfortable and fine for two minutes.

### A trap it would have walked into, caught before the take

`g_in_cockpit` is stamped **inside** `headlook_tick`, after the early return.
With `X4VR_HEADLOOK=0` it would never be stamped, sit at its `false`
initialiser, and bin every cursor change as "elsewhere" — so the scorer would
have printed **NOT ONE CHANGE IN THE COCKPIT for a run spent entirely in the
cockpit**, on the very run built to answer that question, and the answer would
have looked like a confirmation.

A default that cannot be told from a measurement is the defect this file keeps
paying for. There is now a `g_view_known` flag; the census appends **"VIEW
NEVER STAMPED, the split is meaningless"** and the scorer refuses the
cockpit verdict while keeping what still stands — the change and button counts
are real, only WHERE is unknown. Planted in the suite (65 cases) with a check
that the refuted verdict cannot come back.

## P313 — is MOUSELOOK what suppresses cockpit hover? (X4VR_HEADLOOK=0)

Take 312's line **plus `X4VR_HEADLOOK=0`** and nothing else. One variable.
**WiVRn. No emulated pad, real mouse and keyboard.**

### Why this configuration and not a new knob

`may_steer = cockpit && hud` is exactly the condition for holding MOUSELOOK, so
*cockpit + HUD up + key released* is unreachable through any existing release
path. `X4VR_HEADLOOK=0` reaches it: `headlook_tick()` returns before anything is
forced, and `headlook_enabled()` also gates the inputmap rewrite, so
`INPUT_STATE_CAMERA_MOUSELOOK` stays on X4's own binding and nothing of ours
touches it.

**Cost: the view will not follow his head for this run.** Uncomfortable, and
acceptable for two minutes.

### The protocol supplies the attribution the flag cannot

With head-look off, `g_in_cockpit` is never stamped, so the census refuses the
cockpit/elsewhere split (by design — see the `g_view_known` guard). So the
attribution comes from the protocol instead: **do not open the map at all.**
Every cursor change is then a cockpit change by construction.

* **P313.1** `cursor sets` prints and appends **"VIEW NEVER STAMPED, the split
  is meaningless"**, and the scorer refuses the split. **This is the guard
  working, not a failure** — and the change and button counts still stand.
* **P313.2** the cursor **appears in the cockpit without a map visit**. Take
  312 needed one (*"does not appear until I bring up the map and leave it"*),
  and the reason is that X4 had not SET a cursor yet. With MOUSELOOK not held,
  X4 should be in normal pointer mode from the start and set one. If it still
  needs a map visit, that behaviour is NOT a MOUSELOOK artifact and #64 is
  larger than "seed a default cursor".
* **P313.3 — the one that matters.** `changed` well above the button count,
  and Patola sees **arrow -> cross-in-circle over a target**. That would mean
  **holding MOUSELOOK is what suppresses cockpit hover**, #46's cockpit half is
  #71's structure rather than a placement defect, and it cannot be fixed by
  moving the cursor.

### What refutes it, and where that goes

Hover still failing with head-look off. Then MOUSELOOK is **not** the cause and
something in our stack breaks X4's hit-testing regardless — far worse, and the
next step would be **our mod in flatscreen** (injector + layer, `X4VR_VR=0`) to
separate the mod from the VR path, since the vanilla control has already
cleared X4 itself.

### The caveat, stated so a clean result is not over-read

A head-look-OFF run cannot say whether hover would **also** work with head-look
ON. It can only say whether MOUSELOOK is what suppresses it. Those are
different questions and only the second one is being asked.

## Take 313 — SCORED: hover EXISTS with head-look off, and lands in the WRONG PLACE

`X4VR_HEADLOOK=0`, otherwise take 312's line. WiVRn, configuration 1 (no
controllers, real mouse and keyboard). The map was not opened.

    cursor sets   166 set(s), handle found 166, NOT found 0, null 0
                  160 change(s) | 62 mouse button press(es)
    first SET     at the first button press (t=153204); the 0-set line at
                  t=153080 says X4 had built 26 cursors and SET none
    click-free    107 of the 156 changes after the first set fell in 2 s
                  report windows with NO new button press

Patola: *"The cursor was not appearing, it only appeared after I kept the left
mouse button pressed to steer with it. After that, I have noticed that in some
places of the screen it would change the shape to the circle with cross inside.
But it was the wrong area of the screen for the objects, and I could not grasp
the pattern."* The log and his eye agree on both halves: no cursor until the
first press, and shape changes without clicks afterwards.

### Scoreboard

* **P313.1 HELD.** `VIEW NEVER STAMPED` printed; the scorer refused the split.
* **P313.2 REFUTED as written.** No map visit was needed — but a CLICK was. The
  trigger was never the map: it is X4's first `SDL_SetCursor`, which any
  pointer interaction produces. #64 is still "seed a default cursor", and is
  now known not to be a MOUSELOOK artifact.
* **P313.3 HELD in its core, WRONG in its tail.** Hover exists in the cockpit
  with head-look off: cross-in-circle seen, 107 click-free changes. But P313.3
  also said #46's cockpit half *"cannot be fixed by moving the cursor"* — and
  the cross appearing in the wrong area is exactly a placement defect. There
  are TWO things: head-look suppresses hover, and once hover exists it is
  misplaced.

**One caveat on the attribution.** 312 -> 313 changed one KNOB and three
mechanisms with it: the MOUSELOOK hold, the inputmap rewrite, and our
`xrel`/`yrel` drop. "Head-look ON suppresses cockpit hover" is established;
which of the three does it is not.

### The misplacement is take 310's arithmetic, which take 311 could not test

`cursor_canvas()`'s comment derived it at take 310: X4 hit-tests the world at
the RAW pointer `n`, while the canvas draws the cursor at `A·n` with
`A = 0.5252`. So the cross appears when the DRAWN cursor sits at about half the
object's distance from the centre of view — right at the centre, increasingly
wrong toward the edge. That is "the wrong area of the screen" with a pattern
that is hard to see from inside.

Take 311's A/B was built to test exactly this and read null in the cockpit —
**because MOUSELOOK was held in both arms, so neither could show hover at
all.** A test run where the quantity is zero ([[test-the-fix-where-it-can-act]]).
Take 313 is the first run in which cockpit hover exists, so the A/B can now
act. That is P314.

### The design conflict this exposes

Head-look drives X4's camera THROUGH MOUSELOOK (held key plus synthetic motion).
Cockpit hover needs MOUSELOOK released. **In the cockpit, head-look and a
hovering cursor cannot coexist through the current mechanism.** Whatever the
shim does about placement, it will also need a way to hand the pointer over —
e.g. a cursor mode that pauses head-look while the player interacts, the way
vanilla X4 hands the mouse between steering and look. Not designed here; named
so that P314's answer is read as half of the problem.

## Found by the review after take 313

### X4's crash on exit was OURS — fixed

The docs carried *"X4 segfaults on exit in EVERY run... harmless to the data
because it is teardown"*. Nobody had looked at a backtrace. Both X4 cores still
on disk (2026-09-23 23:39, 2026-09-24 00:47) have the same stack:

    #0 IsHUDActive     (X4 + 0x6431d7)
    #1 headlook_tick   (libx4vr_inject.so)
    #2 SDL_PumpEvents  (libx4vr_inject.so — our interposer)

and gdb on the core: `rdx = 0` at `IsHUDActive+7: movzbl 0x418(%rdx),%eax`,
loaded one instruction earlier from the global at `0x3db6e48`. **X4 NULLs its
HUD global during shutdown and keeps pumping events**, while `headlook_tick`
had latched *"once seen alive it stays alive"* — true throughout play, false at
exit. Take 313 is the natural control: head-look off, the call never reached,
and it is the one run with no X4 core (only gamescope's).

Fix: `x4_hud_active()` reads the pointer IsHUDActive is about to dereference
and does not call it while NULL. The address is decoded from IsHUDActive's own
first instruction (`injector/x4vr_riprel.hpp`), refusing anything but the exact
`mov disp32(%rip),%rdx`, so an X4 update that changes the prologue logs that the
guard is off instead of reading a wild address. `tests/riprel.cpp` plants the
refusals and decodes the REAL binary's prologue to `0x3db6e48` — the global the
cores NULLed. **Not yet confirmed in a run**: take 314 runs head-look off and
cannot exercise it; the first head-look-ON take after it can, and should end
with no X4 core in `coredumpctl`.

The lesson is older than this bug: a defect filed as harmless got no backtrace
for weeks, and the backtrace named our code in one line.

`take-221-roll-stereo` was confirmed by take 221 with the pose channel on
(`X4VR_POSE=1`, as in every take 243-256): Patola comfortable at every head
tilt, the control arm comfortable only when level. Take 260 set `X4VR_POSE=0`
as an elimination, which was **withdrawn the same session** (*"the pose channel
was uploading IDENTITY in both runs... the test could only come out one way"*).
The knob stayed. Every canonical line since carries `X4VR_POSE=0`, so
`X4VR_ROLL_STEREO` has patched nothing for about 55 takes, and the scorer's FAIL

**Not restored here, deliberately.** Everything tagged since — `take-268-ui-field`,
`take-274-canvas-far`, `take-303-steamvr` — was established with `X4VR_POSE=0`, so
`X4VR_POSE=1` has never run alongside #76's HUD fix, and the pose channel
carried its own standing FAIL (falls back to identity once after being driven).
Restoring it is a take of its own with one observable — tilt the head: does the

### Instrument and harness defects, all fixed

* **"against a 0x0 eye".** The final cursor census runs at teardown after the
  swapchain chains are gone; take 313's read 0x0, dropped its drawn lines, and
  the scorer (which reads the last line) printed *"SEEN across 0% of the eye"*.
  The layer now keeps the last non-zero extent; the scorer borrows the extent
  from the last census that had one and says so.
* **"CONFINED... This is geometry, not protocol" was false.** It read the DRAWN
  extent, which depends on where the pointer went exactly as the pointer range
  does — take 313 drew 41%x43% under a map whose edge is 52.5%. The layer now
  prints the map's REACHABLE box (its images of the window edges) beside the
  drawn extent; the scorer says CONFINED BY THE MAP only from that box, and
  calls a drawn extent short of it the PROTOCOL. Driven on the GPU in
  `tests/cursor_render.cpp` against an independent computation; the census
  suite plants the swept, unswept, old-log and 0x0 cases.
* **evflow told a mouse take to keep its hands off the mouse.** The note now
  needs something of ours to compete with (pushed > 0.5 Hz).
* **pose said "X4VR_HEADLOOK was not set" when it was set to 0.** Now quotes it.
* **`tests/run-offaxis-bringup.sh` failed 3 cases on its own premise.** It took
  `active_runtime.json` as proof a runtime was up. WiVRn points it at itself
  while running and RESTORES the previous target on exit — here SteamVR's — so
  with nothing running xrCreateInstance hunted a SteamVR that was not there and
  stalled 5.3 s. It now asks for a runtime PROCESS. Its live-runtime cases are
  therefore SKIPPED on an idle machine, not passed: they need WiVRn up to run.
* **Dead code.** `vr_session_thread_started()` and `vr_awaiting_first_view()`
  lost their only caller in `8a22bae` and still carried comments naming it.

## DIRECTIVE CHANGE, 2026-09-26 — a modified game is allowed

Patola: *"I want to be able to fully use X4's lua and modding capabilities with
no reserves, so I am removing the need for avoidance of a 'modified' game... You
are also free to modify our game's configuration (which use different files
than the unmodified game) to enable our mod and deploy new versions when they
appear."*

What this retires: the `modified="0"` constraint on saves, and with it the
reason `x4vr_lua.hpp` gave for Route 1. What it does NOT retire: the player's
own files are still opened read-only and never written — "our game's
configuration" is the forked profile (`config-x4vrmod.xml`,
`inputmap-x4vrmod.xml`). **OpenTrack and X4's head-tracker path stay
forbidden**; this directive says nothing about them.

What it opens, from the files rather than from memory:

* **Situational awareness.** X4 exports view-state queries the injector can
  already call on X4's thread (`IsHUDActive`, `IsExternalViewActive`,
  `IsFloatingViewActive`, `IsInPanelMode`, `IsFullscreenCutsceneActive`,
  `IsMouseSteeringActive`, `IsMouseEmulationActive` …, all declared in X4's own
  cdefs) — that part never needed a modified game. What modding adds is the Lua
  side: X4's UI knows which menu is open and which mode the player is in, and a
  Lua addon can hand that to us through `ffi.C` calling a symbol our
  LD_PRELOADed injector exports. Not built; the bridge is the plan.
* **Protected UI Mode.** X4 refuses non-whitelisted Lua modules while it is on
  (`"Only whitelisted modules are allowed in Protected UI Mode."` in the
  binary). The toggle is `GetUISafeModeOption`/`SetUISafeModeOption`, stored in
  config as `uisafemode` — absent from Patola's `config.xml`, so at its default.
  Our config fork can serve it OFF in memory, touching nothing of vanilla's.
* **Enabling our extensions without touching vanilla.** `content.xml` (which
  extensions are enabled) lives in the SAME profile directory both games read.
  Enabling ours there would enable it for vanilla too. The injector already
  forks `config.xml`; forking `content.xml` the same way — matched by directory,
  since every extension also has a `content.xml` — keeps vanilla untouched.

## Z translation — the state, since it was asked

**Why Z could not be done the way X/Y was.** X4 renders camera-relative, so a
lateral eye shift is exactly a projection shear on what X4 drew
(`x_ndc = sx·(x-d)/z`) — that is how the stereo works. Moving along the view
axis rescales every pixel by `z/(z-dz)`, which depends on each pixel's depth;
there is no single matrix that does it (take 238's analysis).

**And X/Y is off too.** #74's shear was declared at `neutral + R(C)·shift`, a
17 cm lever arm swinging with the camera; take 245 found it was the cause of the
cockpit being "pushed away", the load-screen drift and the wrong-feeling
separation. It has been off since. **No head translation reaches X4 today**;
only yaw and pitch cross the channel.

**Routes, none built:** (1) submit X4's depth with
`XR_KHR_composition_layer_depth` (WiVRn offers it) and let the compositor
reproject with true parallax — costs disocclusion at large leans, plumbing and a
per-frame copy; (2) write `M_view`'s translation so X4 renders from the moved
eye — exact, but X4's CPU culling does not move with it and the block is shared
by 500+ slots. The modding directive adds no third route that I have found:
X4's `playercamera/maxpos` (0.1, 0.1, 0.02) is the G-force sway limit, not a
controllable offset, and the MD camera actions are cutscene cameras. The
head-tracker head-position setters exist and are the forbidden path.

## Head-look and MOUSELOOK — what Patola asked, and what is true

*"Head-look still needs the mouse-look activation? I thought we developed our
own head-look because we wanted to be independent from that."*

**It does.** The servo, the pose read-back and the rendering are ours, but the
actuator is X4's own free-look: we hold `INPUT_STATE_CAMERA_MOUSELOOK` (rebound
to a key of ours) and feed synthetic mouse motion, closed-loop on
`GetCameraRotation`. That was forced, not chosen:

* **No camera setter**, in the C exports or in either Lua bridge — surveyed
  twice ("The Lua route is closed for the camera", and its correction).
* **No other analog look input.** X4's full range vocabulary has only
  `INPUT_RANGE_MOUSELOOK_YAW/PITCH` for free-look (`FP_YAW/PITCH` are walking).
* **The numpad states** (`INPUT_STATE_CAMERA_*`) turn the camera without
  MOUSELOOK but are a **spring** — back to centre within 0.62 s of release, take
  154 — so they cannot hold a pose.
* **Our own viewport** exists — `X4VR_POSE_ROTATE`, takes 186-203 — but X4 culls
  on the CPU against its own frustum, so a rotation of what X4 drew only reaches
  as far as X4 rendered: the seam. To look 60 degrees left, X4's camera has to
  point there.

**His objection to a "cursor mode" is right and it is withdrawn.** The head
moves continuously in VR, including during an interaction; a mode that pauses
head-look to use the pointer would be unusable.

### The door the old survey did not look behind: the camera STATE

The survey looked for setter FUNCTIONS. `GetCameraRotation` itself shows where
the answer lives: root global `0x3db6948` -> object -> camera node at `+0x3e8`
-> an internal call fills the node's rotation matrix -> atan2/asin. So the
free-look angle is state in X4's camera controller, rebuilt into that matrix
each frame. **If the controller keeps it as numbers, writing them each frame is
a camera setter** — no MOUSELOOK, no captured pointer, no input-channel lag, and
possibly past the clamp (which lives in the free-look camera, take 154).

Costs, stated up front:

* **Tied to the X4 build.** Addresses and offsets move with an update. Every
  anchor is decoded from X4's own code and refused if it does not match —
  the same discipline as the IsHUDActive guard.
* **The spring.** Without MOUSELOOK X4 pulls the view home; a write has to beat
  it, either by writing the spring's target as well or by a `parameters.xml`
  change through our extension — allowed now.
* **Timing.** The write must land before X4 builds the frame's camera.

**Step 1 is read-only and built: `X4VR_CAMSCAN=1`** (`injector/x4vr_camscan.hpp`).
Every ~100 ms, on X4's thread, it takes the angle `GetCameraRotation` reports and
the bytes of the objects that function reads — root, camera node, and every
pointer one level deep from the first 1 KB of each — and keeps the slots that
track the angle in radians or degrees, either sign, float or double, across many
DISTINCT angles. All reads go through `process_vm_readv` on our own pid, which
answers an unmapped address with EFAULT instead of a fault. `tests/camscan.cpp`
plants the state, a constant, a `sin(yaw)` and a one-time coincidence, a still
camera, and a state outside the range. It caught a real defect before any take:
discovery was shared between the axes, so a player who turns before he nods
never had pitch collected. Discovery is per axis now.

**Step 0, the premise, is a protocol and costs nothing:** does hover survive a
camera turned WITHOUT MOUSELOOK? Holding a numpad key puts X4 in exactly that
state. If picking follows the turned camera, any non-MOUSELOOK drive keeps the
cursor working. If it does not, a camera write alone would not fix the cursor.

## Head translation — back on, and the combination that could not work

Patola: *"just turn head translation back on. It's important to test with the
cursor... it is a necessary confounding factor since it will be used in
gameplay."* (He had believed our extension helped it; it does not — the
extension only raises the free-look clamp.)

**Found reading the code first: `X4VR_HEAD_TRANSLATE=1` with `X4VR_POSE=0` was a
trap.** The shift reaches the shaders only through the pose channel —
`pose_drive_residual()` returns at once when `!pose_active()` — while the
declared position adds the shift regardless. So the compositor would have been
told the image came from a leaned eye it was never rendered from, and warped a
lean that is not in the picture. The layer now **refuses** the shift in that
combination and logs `head translate: ASKED FOR BUT INACTIVE`; the scorer FAILs
it. Translation therefore needs `X4VR_POSE=1`, which also brings roll stereo
back (off since take 260).

With `X4VR_POSE_ROTATE` unset, the pose channel's residual rotation is written
but no shader reads it, so `X4VR_POSE=1` with head-look off changes exactly two
things: roll stereo and the translation shear.

**Why it was off, so a comfort report can be read:** take 245 removed it and
three complaints improved at once (cockpit pushed away, load-screen drift, eye
separation). Since then the UI quad is gone (the UI is in the eye image at
1000 m), and the declared rotation changed (`DECLARE_RENDERED_ROT=2`). So this
is a re-measurement under a changed configuration, not a known outcome.

**One limit with head-look OFF:** the shift is computed in HEAD axes and applied
in X4's camera axes. With head-look on those agree; with it off, X4's camera
stays forward, so a lean made with the head turned is applied in the wrong
direction. Face forward for this take. With head-look on, or once the camera is
driven directly, the two agree again.

### Two defects of mine, found by this take's own output

### camscan: a BOUNDED null, and the disassembly says why

    1455 samples, yaw swept 128 deg, pitch 40 deg, 50 regions / 112 KB
    discoveries 140, eliminated 119+, SURVIVORS 0

Read the instrument before the null ([[state-the-instrument-range]]):

* **The sweep happened only in the last ~35 s** (the numpad part), and in that
  window candidates were discovered and eliminated 61 times. That is the
  signature of slots that match at rest and at the stops but MISS during the
  fast transit (92 deg/s): a stored TARGET angle (+-65 while the key is held,
  0 when released), or a value one frame out of step with the matrix. The 0.05
  degree tolerance discards both. So this refutes only "an angle stored in step
  with the rendered camera, in these objects".
* **The camera's orientation is a MATRIX in per-frame buffers.**
  GetCameraRotation's internal call (`0x1925bf0`) picks a buffer index from a
  THREAD-LOCAL flag (`%fs:...`, then one of two globals), walks a 0x50-byte-entry
  list inside the camera object at `0x30 + idx*0x2c0`, and multiplies by the
  entry's 3x3 rows at +0x20/+0x30/+0x40 plus translation at +0x10. So X4 keeps
  the camera transform per thread/frame, as matrices; the free-look state that
  produces them lives in the controller, elsewhere. Writing the matrices
  directly would race X4's own buffering — not a route.

### The next probe, not built: catch the WRITER

`perf_event_paranoid` is 2, so a process may put a hardware WRITE watchpoint on
its own memory (`perf_event_open`, `PERF_TYPE_BREAKPOINT`, user-space only),
one event per X4 thread. Armed on the camera entry's rotation rows, it reports
the instruction pointer of whatever writes them — the free-look controller's
code — and that function's disassembly names where the state lives, in
whatever representation. Read-only, and it survives the representation
question that defeated the value scan. A lag-and-target-tolerant rescan of
dumped snapshots is the fallback.

## X4VR_CAMWATCH — built, and what driving it for real caught first

`injector/x4vr_camwatch.hpp`, `tests/camwatch.cpp`. Read-only hardware
WRITE watchpoints (`perf_event_open`, `PERF_TYPE_BREAKPOINT`, user space) on
the first rotation row of the key-0 transform entry GetCameraRotation reads,
in every per-frame buffer that looks valid (up to the 4 debug registers a
thread has). X4's thread works out WHERE, once a second, through anchors
decoded from X4's code — the call at GetCameraRotation+0x5d must land on a
function whose first 162 bytes match X4 9.00's byte for byte, or it REFUSES.
OUR thread arms, drains and logs; nothing of ours runs in X4's threads.

The test drives a real watchpoint on a writer, a decoy writer and a reader.
Three defects, all caught before any take:

* **Samples under-counted silently.** A 32 KB ring holds ~74 samples; 1000
  stores produced 74 samples and "lost 0", because the kernel only writes a
  LOST record when there is room for it. The exact number now comes from the
  events' own counters (`read()`), samples are what fit.
* **Locked memory.** Rings count against `perf_event_mlock_kb` (516 KB here)
  per CPU plus `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`; a ring per X4 thread per target would run out
  partway and leave later threads silently unwatched. Every thread now gets a
  COUNTING event (no ring); only threads whose counter moves are upgraded to
  SAMPLING, the count carried across. The test checks only the writer is
  upgraded and the total stays exact (2000 of 2000 across the upgrade).
* **Only the two NAMED buffers were watched.** If X4 triple-buffers, the
  writer fills one neither index global names yet — a clean null over a store
  next door. Every valid buffer is watched now.

## Take 316 — SCORED: one instruction writes the camera; the exit crash moved one call over

Head-look ON, `X4VR_CAMWATCH=1`, translation and pose channel on. PASS. The
milestone fired within seconds of reaching the cockpit (300 samples come fast
at ~120 stores/s). Patola: *"Turning the head was comfortable and working as
before"* — head translation with head-look ON, the regime take 245 had switched
off, gave no complaint (leans to 5.2 cm published).

    anchors        OK, signature-verified
    aimed          2 valid buffers (0 and 1); the index globals both named 1
    events         78 counting, 2 upgraded to sampling, 0 arm failures
    stores         2582 counted, 2565 sampled, 0 LOST
    writers        ONE: ip 0x192a3da, thread 'Movement worker', both buffers

**P316.1 held. P316.2 held, including the prediction that hop 1 is a generic
copy.** The store is `movaps %xmm0,0x20(%rax)` at 0x192a3d6 inside
**0x192a310**, a per-frame snapshot: it clears the buffer's list, reads X4's
current time, calls **0x1929f70(camera, &m, 0, time)** to evaluate the camera's
transform, and appends it as entry key 0. `rbx` held the camera object.

### Hop 2, read statically — where the orientation is built

* **0x1929f70** — a mode switch on camera+0x880 (0 in the cockpit, from the
  core). Evaluates the attached object (+0x780) at `time`, then — with a
  special branch when the camera is the PLAYER's (root+0x3e8) — takes the
  controller at **camera+0x18** and calls its virtual at vtable+0x138. The
  writer's stack held 0x192a096, the return address of that call.
* The controller's vtable is **0x3b81fe0** (read from take 316's core, and
  confirmed against the file: X4 is non-PIE, so vtables are build constants).
  +0x138 is a trampoline (0x1918640) to **+0x1b0 = 0x191d0f0**.
* **0x191d0f0** builds the local transform: the controller's stored matrix
  (+0x10..+0x40), then a CHAIN of child controllers (vector at +0xa0..+0xa8,
  each composed through its own vtable+0x138), then angles extracted with
  atan2/asin and scaled by a factor from this+0x78, plus a translation from a
  global object at **0x3db83c8** (+0x5e0).
* **0x3db83c8 is NOT the head tracker**, as far as the exports say: of every
  exported camera, cockpit and head-tracker function, only
  **GetFollowCameraBasePos** reads it. It is the follow-camera settings object
  (`menu_followcamera.lua`). The forbidden path is not being approached.

So the free-look state is in the controller or one of its children. **Next
probe (hop 2), not built:** log the children's vtables (class identity, build
constants) and watch each child's stored matrix row; the child whose matrix
moves with the head is free-look, and its writer's code names the state.

**A lead, recorded and NOT pursued:** `SetFollowCameraBasePos(Coord3D)` is an
exported setter of a camera base POSITION that this very function adds into the
camera's translation. The Lua cdefs define it (`menu_followcamera.lua`). If it
applied in the cockpit it would be X4 rendering a head translation itself, Z
included — but it is most likely the EXTERNAL follow camera's, scaled by a
factor that is zero in the cockpit. One experiment decides it, later.

### P316.3 FAILED — the exit crash moved to IsInPanelMode

    #0 IsInPanelMode+7  mov 0x8(%rax),%rdx   rax=0
    #1 headlook_tick
    #2 SDL_PumpEvents (ours)

The IsHUDActive guard held; the crash moved ONE CALL OVER. IsInPanelMode loads
its global and dereferences it unchecked — it null-checks the second pointer
only — and **this file's code comment had declared it safe**. The same rule at
a second site ([[fixed-one-site-left-its-twin]]).

Fixed: IsInPanelMode is guarded the same way. And the rule is now a test,
`tests/run-x4-call-guards.sh`: it disassembles every X4 function the injector
calls, follows each global it loads, and FAILS if one is dereferenced before
being tested without an `X4GUARD:` tag in the injector. Of the six: IsHUDActive
and IsInPanelMode unguarded (both tagged now), GetCameraRotation,
IsExternalViewActive and IsFloatingViewActive guarded, IsGamePaused passes a
static object. Its own controls caught two defects in it before it was
trusted: a parser that classified everything as "no load" (objdump's
colon-TAB), and a 0x40-byte window that cut GetCameraRotation's `test` in half
and called a seen-but-unresolved load "no load" — now UNDECIDED, which fails.
Limit: it checks the prologue's global loads, not what IsGamePaused's callee
does inside.

## X4VR_CAMWATCH=2 (hop 2) — built; P317

`X4VR_CAMWATCH=1` stays take 316's hop 1, byte for byte. `=2` aims at the
camera controller instead: seven analysed code sites must match X4 9.00 byte
for byte (the controller at camera+0x18 in both branches of 0x1929f70, the
chain's +0xa0/+0xa8 and the stored matrix +0x10/+0x20 in 0x191d0f0, and the
base compose's row 0), and the controller's vtable+0x1b0 must BE 0x191d0f0, or
it refuses. Each second it reads the chain and logs it whenever it changes —
controller, and per child its object, vtable, compose (vt+0x138) and local
(vt+0x1b0) targets, all build constants for offline disassembly. It watches
stored row 0 of the controller and the first three children (four debug
registers), with hop 1's counting-then-sampling machinery.

**New: a co-movement census**, on X4's thread at 30 Hz: for each watched
matrix, the ticks the CAMERA moved (GetCameraRotation, >0.01 deg — a
"visible" threshold would have scored the free-look matrix as moving alone on
every slow drift), the ticks the matrix moved WITH it, and ALONE. The scorer
calls each MOVES WITH THE CAMERA (free-look candidate), STATIC, ON ITS OWN
(shake/sway), MIXED, or NOT EXERCISED. Paced by its own milestone: every
matrix 60 s of ticks with 10 s of camera motion (hop 1's 300-sample milestone
fired within seconds in take 316, far too early for a census).

`tests/camwatch.cpp`: sites verified against the real binary and a one-byte
change refused and named; a synthetic controller with four children yields
exactly the controller plus three; a foreign controller class and an
end-before-begin vector refuse. Census suite 111 -> 117.

## Take 317 — SCORED: the controller's matrix is the SWAY, not free-look; X4 exits clean

`X4VR_CAMWATCH=2`, head-look ON. PASS (after the scorer fixes below).

    chain       controller vtable 0x3b81fe0, local 0x191d0f0, 2 children
                (both class vt 0x3b96650, local 0x191d790)
    writer      ONE: ip 0x1e02395, 'Movement worker', writing the controller's
                stored matrix; returns into 0x191d5c8 (0x191d0f0's update branch)
    census      controller  WITH 1342 / camera 1983, ALONE 26, max 9.3 deg
                child0/1    STATIC, a fixed 57.3 deg (1 rad) rotation each
    camera      yaw span 131 deg

* **P317.1 held.** A camera of ANOTHER class (vtable 0x3b59bc8, local
  0x19186a0 — the load/menu camera) was refused first; the cockpit's verified
  40 s later. Correct behaviour, and the scorer FAILED the run on it — fixed:
  a refused CLASS is transient; only a run that never verified fails, and a
  CODE mismatch always does.
* **P317.2 did NOT hold as posed.** The census called the controller "MIXED" —
  it co-moves with the camera — but its rotation never passed **9.3 degrees**
  while the head swung the camera through **131**. It is X4's G-force
  SWAY/inertia (`playercamera` in parameters.xml), not free-look. **My census
  could not tell them apart**: under head-look the camera moves on 84% of
  ticks, so anything that changes often "moves with" it. HOW FAR was missing.
  The census now logs each matrix's maximum rotation (displacement for a
  translation), and the scorer calls one "TOO SMALL to be the free-look" when
  it stays under a quarter of the camera's half-span; take 317 rescored:
  *"moves, but only up to 9.3 deg against the camera's +-66 — TOO SMALL"*.
  Older logs get the angle estimated from the logged 3x3 ranges.
* **P317.3, read statically, names the sway:** the update branch
  (0x191d4f0, when time has advanced) asks the attached object for its motion
  (vtable+0x260), computes dt, and calls **0x13f1970(settings+0x540,
  &stored matrix, &state +0x80, &motion, dt, param)** — a physics step writing
  the stored matrix. Consistent with sway, not look-around.
* **P317.4 HELD: no X4 core.** First head-look-ON run to exit clean; only
  gamescope's own teardown crash, present on every run and not ours.

### Where free-look must be, and hop 2b

Not the controller's stored matrix (sway), not the children (static). What
0x191d0f0 has left: the transform on the object at global **0x3db83c8**
(translation +0x5e0, rotation rows +0x5f0..), whose Euler angles it extracts,
scales by a factor from this+0x78, and composes. **Not the head tracker**: all
of X4's head-tracker exports use other globals (0x3db8938, 0x3daab80, ...); of
the camera exports only GetFollowCameraBasePos reads 0x3db83c8.

**`X4VR_CAMWATCH=3` (hop 2b), built:** four more code sites verified (the
global's own `mov disp32(%rip),%r14`, whose displacement gives 0x3db83c8, and
the +0x5f4/+0x604/+0x5e0 reads); watches and censuses `settings.rot`
(+0x5f0), `settings.pos` (+0x5e0) and the controller's sway as reference.

## Our extension enabled for the modded session — X4VR_EXTENSIONS=1

Patola, before take 318: *"our X4 extension for adjustments (allowing 360°
and fixing the shadows issue) is not activated. For the next runs I would
prefer that the extension is activated."*

* **The extension does ONE thing**: cockpit free-look limits 65/35 -> 180/75.
  **Nothing addresses the shadows** — #70 is parked as X4's own wide-field
  cascade defect (takes 224-228). Modding being allowed now could reopen it
  through parameters.xml; nothing has been tried.
* **Source of truth moved into the repo**: `extension/x4vrmod_lookaround/`,
  with the stale "65/35 to 85/85" description corrected to 180/75.
* **`launch/deploy-extensions.sh`**, called by the launcher under
  `X4VR_EXTENSIONS=1`, copies our directories into X4's `extensions/` only when
  they differ, touches nothing else, and says what it did.
* **The injector forks `content.xml`** (`injector/x4vr_content.hpp`) exactly as
  it forks config.xml: seeded once from the player's file, served with our
  extension forced `enabled="true"` in memory, writes redirected to
  `content-x4vrmod.xml`. Matched by directory, so extension manifests pass
  through. Served on BOTH the fopen and open() read paths, since nothing on
  record says which X4 uses; the log names it.
* `tests/run-content-fork.sh` drives the REAL injector without X4 (`cat` via
  open(), `sed` via fopen()): enabled on both paths, the player's file
  byte-identical, writes landing in the fork, manifests untouched, nothing at
  all with the knob off. Its first draft assumed `cat` used openat — the
  injector's log said open(), and the test was wrong, not the hook.
* **Head-look must be told too**: the servo clamps its own target at 65/35
  unless `X4VR_HEADLOOK_YAW_LIMIT=180 X4VR_HEADLOOK_PITCH_LIMIT=75` (take 211
  reached 177.98/75.00 that way). The launcher warns when the extension is on
  and the limit is not.
* Scorer: `extensions` block, FAIL if asked for and X4 never read content.xml

## Hop 3 — the camera's own transform (`X4VR_CAMWATCH=4`), built

Re-reading **0x1929f70** past the controller call: after composing the
controller's local transform (0x192a096..0x192a15a), it composes **one more
transform, the camera object's own**: `movaps 0x5a0/0x5b0/0x5c0/0x5d0(%rbx)` —
translation then three rotation rows — on every mode's path, the cockpit's
(mode 0) included. Then it returns. Nothing watched it:
* hop 2/2b read the controller and the settings object only;
* take 315's value scan read the camera's first KB; +0x5a0 is past it.

Writers exist statically: 0x1935a25..0x1935a4b stores all four rows and then
tests `0x880(%r15)` (the mode field — so r15 is a camera), 0x192edc3..
0x192edd8 stores them beside +0x868. One of those, or neither, is free-look;
the watch says which.

What remains of 0x1929f70 after this: the attached object (camera+0x780,
evaluated by **0x18a0090**) — composed FIRST. If the camera's own transform is
static, that is the last link.

**`X4VR_CAMWATCH=4`:** six sites verified against X4 9.00 (the player's-camera
test, the mode load, the four row loads); it does NOT need the controller's
class — the controller's sway is added as the reference when verified (the
census's positive control: take 318 saw it written). Targets: `camera.rot`
(+0x5b0), `camera.pos` (+0x5a0), `controller`. The camera's address, mode and
starting transform are logged when it changes.

**The sharper question: does its angle EQUAL the camera's?** On every census
tick with GetCameraRotation at least 10° off centre ("far"), |angle(matrix) −
angle(camera)| goes in a 1° histogram. The angle of a yaw-then-pitch rotation
is the same in either composition order with roll zero, so no convention is
guessed: cos θ = (cos y + cos p + cos y cos p − 1)/2 (tests/camwatch.cpp checks
both orders against explicit matrices). The free-look has the camera's angle up
to sway and a frame of lag; the sway does not. Every 5 s with the camera ≥30°
off centre, one raw (yaw, pitch, roll | rows) pair is logged, so the convention
for a WRITE can be read off offline. Milestone: the old 60 s/10 s, plus 10 s of
"far" ticks.

Scorer: `HAS THE CAMERA'S ANGLE` (median ≤3°, p90 ≤10°, ≥300 far ticks),
`does NOT have` (median >10°), `PARTLY` (read the samples), `NOT EXERCISED`;
FAIL if hop 3 was asked and the camera transform never censused. Census suite
126 → 140.

## 0x1933d00, read: X4 keeps the free-look IN THE MATRIX, and a spring pulls it home

Static reading only; no run. All addresses X4 9.00.

**Caller.** The per-frame caller (0xfeaff0, call at 0xfeb806) passes the
player's camera (root+0x3e8) and its inputs:
* xmm0..xmm5: digital camera axes built from input-state bits at
  [0x3daab80]+0x32c (±1.0 per held key — the numpad camera keys);
* esi: a byte at [0x3daab80]+0x360, xmm6/xmm7: floats at +0x364/+0x368, read
  under a mutex at +0x330 and **zeroed after reading** — accumulated mouse-look
  deltas and their "mouse-look active" flag;
* 0xfec0db, 0x1d7dde1, 0x1d7e3f3, 0x1d7e890 call it with all inputs zero
  (resets on camera changes; 0x1d7e3f3 first stores +0x5a0..+0x5d0 itself).

**0x1933d00, cockpit path (mode +0x880 == 0):**
1. If the object at [0x3db8938]+0x148 reports itself active, it branches to
   0x1935ac1, which reads `trackmaxpitch`/`trackmaxyaw` — **X4's head-tracker
   path. Not used, not touched.**
2. Otherwise it re-bases the camera's stored local transform (+0x5a0..+0x5d0)
   against a base (+0x6f0..+0x720, composed with the attached object), and
   **extracts yaw/pitch from the stored matrix** (call 0xb08290 at 0x19342f8).
   The matrix IS the state; there is no separate angle variable.
3. **Mouse-look flag set** (0x19344a4): yaw += mouse delta, pitch += mouse
   delta, clamped to ±maxyaw/±maxpitch; no spring.
   **Flag clear** (0x1935f03): target = numpad axis × max (zero with no key),
   and **0x1e8c260 → 0x1a482d0**, a speed- and acceleration-limited follower
   (`anglespeed`, `angleacc`), moves the angle toward it, velocities kept at
   +0x750/+0x754. That is the numpad's snap to the extremes and its return
   home (take 154's "spring", 0.62 s).
4. **0x1e02200** rebuilds the rotation rows at +0x5b0 from the angles (its
   store at 0x1e02395 is take 319's writer #2 — the same routine the sway
   uses), then the base is composed back in and +0x5a0..+0x5d0 stored
   (0x193462a, 0x1934653).

**The parameters object 0x3db83c8** (called "follow-camera settings" above —
it is the player-camera parameters) holds `<lookaround><internal>` in
attribute order: maxpitch +0x688, maxyaw +0x68c, anglespeed +0x690, angleacc
+0x694, trackmaxpitch +0x698, trackmaxyaw +0x69c (each confirmed by the code
that reads it).

**The follower with `anglespeed` 0:** 0x1a482d0 treats |maxspeed| < 1e-4
(constant at 0x2e25d80) as "desired velocity zero" — guarded, no division —
so the angle STAYS where it is. Overshoot snapping cannot fire at zero
velocity.

**The convention**, fitted to take 319's raw samples (yaw ψ, pitch θ as
GetCameraRotation reports them, radians; roll 0):

    row0 = ( cos ψ,          0,      −sin ψ        )
    row1 = (−sin ψ · sin θ,  cos θ,  −cos ψ · sin θ )
    row2 = ( sin ψ · cos θ,  sin θ,   cos ψ · cos θ )

Checked on three samples to 3 decimals (e.g. ψ −28.77, θ 9.8 → rows (0.8766 0
0.4812 | 0.0819 0.9854 −0.1492 | −0.4742 0.1702 0.8638)).

### The write this makes possible — head-look WITHOUT MOUSELOOK (proposed)

* A second extension, enabled only for the write test, sets `<internal
  anglespeed="0">`: the follower holds the angle, so a matrix written into
  camera+0x5b0 stays. Side effect, stated: the numpad camera keys stop turning
  the cockpit view in that mode (they only steer the follower's target).
* The injector writes the head's yaw/pitch as the matrix above each tick —
  absolute, no servo loop, no MOUSELOOK key, no synthetic mouse. X4 extracts it,
  the follower leaves it, X4 rebuilds the same matrix. A write landing inside
  X4's read-modify-write is lost for one frame, not accumulated.
* Refuses unless: the sites verify; mode 0; the base transform is identity
  (else compose with it); the parameters object reads anglespeed 0 and the
  limits our extension set (75/180, which also confirms the layout live).
* Take 315 proved hover works with the camera turned without MOUSELOOK, so the
  cursor should need no correction.

**The shadow side next**, by Patola's instruction not to defer it far: the
shadow-configured camera slots pinned at sx 1.33333 (take 223) — find the
code that sets them the same way: watch, catch the writer, read it.

## X4VR_HEADLOOK_WRITE=1 — head-look without MOUSELOOK, built

Patola: *"Yes, build the write test."* The first WRITE into X4's memory.

* **`injector/x4vr_camwrite.hpp`**: twelve code sites verified byte for byte
  (the parameters global's load, the extract and rebuild calls, the mouse-look
  branch, the four parameter loads, the follower's zero-speed guard, the base
  loads) on top of hop 3's six; X4's loaded parameters checked live —
  maxpitch/maxyaw must read our 75/180 (degrees or radians, said which), which
  also confirms the field layout, and **anglespeed must read 0**; the camera's
  base (+0x6f0..) must be identity; mode 0. Any miss: REFUSED, said once per
  reason, counted.
* **The convention, against X4's own matrices**: tests/camwrite.cpp rebuilds
  all nine entries of all thirteen of take 319's stored matrices from their two
  angles — worst entry error 0.00007 — and checks the yaw sign against
  GetCameraRotation (within sway, 4.6 deg worst).
* **The write**: every head-look tick in the cockpit (HUD up), the head's
  yaw/pitch → rows → camera+0x5b0, w kept, through `process_vm_writev` (tested
  here: it lands on ourselves, and a freed address is EFAULT, not a crash). No
  servo, no lead, no MOUSELOOK key, no mouse delta. Yaw faded near the vertical
  exactly as the servo's was; the 180 limit wraps, as X4 does.
* **Steering** in write mode means "the write is allowed this tick", not
  relative mouse mode (which never comes), so the layer's declared pose stays
  live. The HUD gate asks IsHUDActive directly (its NULL guard decoded), since
  the MOUSELOOK path's latch never sets.
* **`extension/x4vrmod_headlook`**: `anglespeed` 200 → 0. `enabled="0"` in its
  manifest; the launcher deploys it ONLY for a write session and removes our
  copy otherwise (`deploy-extensions.sh --without`); the content fork forces it
  on with the knob and OFF without it (X4 writes content.xml into the fork, so
  one write session would otherwise leave it on). Tested both ways.
* **Scorer `hwrite`**: armed/refusals, writes, MOUSELOOK presses (FAIL if any),
  extension served (FAIL if not), **tracking** — |X4 − head| over cockpit
  lagsamples while writing — and **hover** from the cursor census. Servo-rate
  blocks carry a note that they describe a servo this run did not use. Census
  suite +9.

**The baseline**, the same tracking statistic on MOUSELOOK head-look:

    take 320  |X4 - head| yaw median 0.25 p90 1.63 deg, pitch 0.17 / 0.87
    take 318                          0.30      1.67           0.19 / 0.78
