## #70, the field X4 sizes things by — read statically, and an A/B to switch it

No run. Patola: *"switch the sway off in the extension, then the shadow hunt."*

**X4's FOV option is a MULTIPLIER on a compiled-in default.** The Lua
`GetFOVOption` (0xab4010, registered at 0xa6da51) reads key `fov` from the
options object at [0x3daab80]+0x150 (getter 0x1fb90e0, default 1.0). Two
camera set-up sites read it:

    0x137340c / 0x138b9ca:  camera+0x874 = max(option, 0.01) x base
                            (base = camera+0x890 at the second site)

and the camera constructor (0x1dcca31/0x1dcca39) sets **both** +0x874 and
+0x890 from the constant at **0x2e2cbc4 = 1.2870022 rad = 73.74°**. Nothing
else ever writes +0x890. So:

    camera+0x874   EFFECTIVE   option x 73.74  = 110° at X4VR_FOV 1.4917
    camera+0x890   BASE        73.74° always   = sx 1.33333

**That is the pinned population's field exactly** (take 223: all 58
shadow-configured slots at sx 1.33333, the rendering slots following
`<fov>`). Readers of the BASE:

* **0x19276fc**: camera+0x890 → a view's +0xcc8, then 0x21bc1b0, which builds
  that view's projection from it (mode ≤ 4) — a view at 73.74° while the
  picture is 110°;
* **0x1164da3**: right after the camera-rotation fetch (0x1925bf0, the one
  GetCameraRotation uses), tan(base/2) — a frustum extent at 73.74°;
* 0x128f066 (another view, via 0x21bc990) and 0x2a3f45b (a copy of the
  camera's fields).

Readers of the EFFECTIVE: 0x1926f80/0x1927010 (returned to callers),
0x17572fd, 0x175790b, 0xaec1f0.

**Hypothesis, not established:** the cascade fit is sized by a BASE-field view,
so at 110° the outer pixels fall outside the cascade boxes and their shadow
weights fade — the take-228 knee (1.24 clean, 1.28 fading) being where the
cascade boxes' margins run out. Widening the base to the rendered field should
make the two agree.

**`X4VR_SHADOWFOV_AB=<seconds>`** switches it live (injector/x4vr_shadowfov.hpp):
CONTROL phases leave X4's default base, FIX phases write camera+0x890 =
option × 73.74°, each switch announced by notification. Seven code sites and
the constant verified byte for byte; the camera's fields must read as the
layout says (default base, option × default effective) before anything is
written. X4's setter recomputes the effective as option × base on a camera
re-init, which from a widened base would compound to 164°; the effective is
restored to the rendered field whenever it drifts. tests/shadowfov.cpp: 17
checks. Scorer `shadowfov`: armed, phases, writes, restores, frame time per
phase.

**Side effects to watch, stated before the run:** if any system other than the
shadows is sized by the base — the HUD layout (#45: X4 lays its UI out against
the DEFAULT field), LOD, the cockpit displays (0x128f066's view) — it will
change in FIX phases too. A HUD that resizes or slides in FIX would say the
base is shared, and the fix must then target the shadow view alone.

### What X4's shaders say the shadow lookup uses

`l_pass_globallight.frag.glsl` (re-extracted to /tmp/x4-shadersrc) lights with
`view_pos = UnProject(...)` (M_invprojection) but looks up the cascades with
`view_pos_uj = UnProjectUJ(clip − jitter)` (**M_invprojection_uj**), then
`coords[i] = view_pos_uj × M_shadowCSMi` and the fade on `length(view_pos_uj)`
(common_frag.glsl `global_lights`). So the shadows have their own inverse
projection. Take 318's camdiff saw M_projection and M_projection_uj change on
the same 1.2% of frames by the same maximum, which suggests the unjittered
pair is the wide one — not yet compared by value. And take 266's
`csm0-scale` read 0.154204 (≈6.5 m) in every view-space slot and frame: a
constant cascade-0 box, suggesting a fixed-size (stable, sphere-fitted)
cascade — whose size may come from a field other than the one rendered.

## Our libraries have no exit-time destructors any more (the gamescope abort of take 323)

The mechanism, reproduced before fixing:

* gamescope destroys its image views from its **own** exit-time destructors.
* Our layer is dlopen'ed during `vkCreateInstance`, after gamescope's globals
  were built. Its static tables were therefore registered later and destroyed
  **first**.
* `x4vr_DestroyImageView` then ran `g_devices.at()` on a destroyed map. It
  threw `std::out_of_range`, and an exception leaving a Vulkan entry point is
  `std::terminate`.

`tests/exit_teardown.cpp` repeats that pattern: a global built before main()
destroys an image view, an image, its memory, the device and the instance from
its destructor. Against 71fe6e7's layer it dies with *"terminate called after
throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range' / what(): unordered_map::at"*, as
gamescope and as X4 alike (with no X4VR_LOG it segfaults instead). Against the
fixed layer it exits 0.

The rule is wider than one hook. Any call into our code after exit() begins
reads freed tables. That includes the injector's interposed libc functions
(close, fclose, mmap), whose function-local statics were registered at first
use. Before the fix the layer registered 73 exit-time destructors and the
injector 31. The fix is `common/x4vr_immortal.hpp`: `x4vr::immortal<T>()`
builds each table on zeroed storage that is never freed, so it starts exactly
as a static would and is never destroyed:

* 44 namespace-scope tables and 7 structs (g_sbs, g_track, g_variants,
  g_pose, g_probe, g_burst, g_vrs) in the layer;
* 8 function-local statics in the layer (including the X4VR_TEST_HAMMER
  thread);
* 4 globals, 6 function-local statics and the config header's 11 strings and
  2 tables in the injector;
* one never-used `static std::vector<bool> dummy` in the injector's
  SDL_GetKeyboardState hook, deleted.

`tests/run-no-exit-destructors.sh` checks both libraries:

* **Static:** no call or tail jump to `__cxa_atexit`. Its control is a
  one-map library, which must count. That control caught my first counter,
  which looked for `call` only and missed tail jumps.
* **Runtime:** the teardown test with no layer, as gamescope, and as X4.
* **Old-layer control:** `X4VR_OLD_LAYER=<old build>/layer` adds the case
  that must fail.

Why takes 314–322 escaped is not known. Whether gamescope exits through its
destructors or through a signal likely depends on how X4 quits.

## #70's cause, read from X4's code: the cascade fit sizes its spheres by 1/tan of the half-field

No run. Patola: *"go ahead with the cascade fit read."* New tools:
`tools/xref.py` (code and data references to an address or string, plus direct
calls) and `tools/xdisp.py` (every `[reg + disp]` use of a displacement).
Each byte-pattern hit is attributed to an instruction by majority vote over 32
linear decodes. Both first versions decoded backwards from the displacement
and read `f3 0f 11 83 74 08 00 00` (movss) as `11 83 ...` (adc), so the vote
is validated against the known +0x874 sites. xdisp also found a reader the
previous search missed (0x1939ef5, cvtss2sd).

**Where.** The fit is 0x2094fc0, called once (0x20d203a) with the main
rendering view. It reads that view's field at view+0xcc8, which is why take
323's cascades followed the live switch. X4's shader-parameter name tables
(.data.rel.ro 0x3bac400..) name what it feeds: `csmthresholds` (vector 14),
`shadowmaxdistance`/`shadowmapsize` (scalars 14/16), `shadowCSM0..4`
(matrices 6–10).

**What.** For each cascade i, over a slice [n, f] of view depth:

    sx, sy = (1 / tan(field/2)) / aspect      aspect = [0x4533b00], [0x4533b04], 1.0 for a square render
    r^2    = ((f - n)/2)^2 + (f/2 * sx)^2 + (f/2 * sy)^2
    centre = the slice's middle on the view axis (texel-snapped)
    threshold_i = (n + f)/2 + sqrt(3) * r        -> csmthresholds
    ortho box half-width = r

* Cascade 0 is n = 0.1 to f = 3.0 × 1.02 ([0x45343ec] × 1.02).
* Cascades 1–4 come from a log/linear blend (`powf`) between 3.0 and the
  maximum distance.

**Checked against every cascade number we have:**

    field    cascade-0 1/r  predicted / measured     threshold 0  predicted / measured
    73.74°   0.30841 / 0.30841 (take 323, menu)       7.20 / 7.2   (takes 190–202)
    91.44°   0.38800 / 0.38799 (take 323, B)          —
    110°     0.47215 / 0.47213 (take 323, A)          5.25 / 5.2   (takes 190–202)
    129.0°   0.55441 / —                              4.70 / 4.7   (take 200)

**Why the shadows fade.**

* The slice's half-extent at its far end is f·tan(field/2) = f/sx. X4 uses
  f·sx/2.
* The two agree only at sx = √2 (70.5°). Call the coverage ratio
  ρ = (sx/2)/tan(field/2) = sx²/2: 0.889 at X4's 73.74°, 0.663 at vanilla's
  81.9°, 0.475 at 91.44° (take 320 VR and take 323 B: **clean**), 0.429 at
  94.4° (take 228's 1.28: **fading**), and 0.245 at our 110° (**fading**).
* The knee Patola located by eye is this ratio crossing ~0.45.
* For a wide field the cockpit reach scales with ρ·f, independent of the
  field. A corner surface leaves cascade 0's full-weight zone (the tent's inner
  2/3) at roughly 2ρf/3 ≈ 0.5 m at 110°, against ≈ 1.35 m in vanilla. Hence
  "the corners immediately", and yaw and pitch alike.

The defect is X4's own (take 226, no layer) and invisible at the fields X4
ships with.

**Levers.**

* **(A) Write X4's aspect globals** [0x4533b00/04]. They are also the default
  x/y scale of every projection built without one of its own (0x21bbf80,
  0x21bc7d7 and two more in the view class), so the picture or other views
  could change. Not surgical, and which views rely on the default is unknown.
* **(B) Give the fit its own divisors.** Four instructions read the aspect
  globals inside the fit, at 0x209539f, 0x20953c8, 0x2095554 and 0x2095577
  (`cvtss2sd xmmN, [rip+disp32]`). Retargeting their four displacements at a
  private pair of floats, mapped within ±2 GB of X4's code, changes the fit
  and nothing else. It would be patched once at injector start, before X4's
  threads exist. The 21bbf80 call inside the fit keeps X4's own values: that
  call builds the slice's perspective, which is correct. Divisor
  d = sx²/(2ρ) gives any ρ; CONTROL is d = X4's own value. This is the first
  write to X4's code rather than its data, so it is Patola's decision.
* **(C) Rewrite the formula.** More bytes and no gain over (B).
* **The shader cannot fix it.** A cascade has no shadow data outside its box.

**What a ρ costs.** Cascade 0 at 110° covers more metres with the same
2048-texel tile:

    rho     divisor   box (m)   cascade-0 sx   reach (full weight, corners)
    0.245   1.0       4.23      0.47229        ~0.5 m   (now)
    0.475   0.516     6.58      0.30417        ~1.0 m   (= 91.44°, judged clean)
    0.663   0.370     8.71      0.22954        ~1.35 m  (= vanilla 81.9°, whose box is 5.80 m)
    1.0     0.245     12.71     0.15736        the whole slice

The wider field costs sharpness, and that cost belongs to 110° itself. Vanilla
pays 5.80 m for its 81.9°.

## X4VR_CSM_COVER — #70's fix, built (Patola: "Patch the 4 reads", coverage "Vanilla's, 0.663")

Patola chose lever (B) on 2026-10-06. This is the project's first write to
X4's code.

* **The patch.** `injector/x4vr_csmfit.hpp` holds the four sites
  (0x209539f, 0x20953c8, 0x2095554, 0x2095577: `cvtss2sd xmmN,
  [rip+disp32]`), each byte-verified and each required to point at its aspect
  global. X4's default aspect constant (1, 1) at 0x2e24680 is checked too. A
  private page is mapped below X4's image base (0x3f0000 by
  `MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE`) and the four displacements are rewritten to point at
  it. The page is made writable for the copy, returned to r-x, and read back.
* **When.** In the injector's constructor in X4's process, before any X4 code
  has run, so no thread can be inside those instructions. Anything that does
  not match refuses with a milestone, and X4's fit is left untouched.
* **The tick.** Each tick (X4's event drain) sets the private pair to X4's own
  aspect values (CONTROL) or to d = cot²/(2ρ·a) (FIX), with the field read
  from camera+0x874. The tick logs the coverage and the cascade-0 sx X4's
  formula predicts for the arm in force. `X4VR_CSM_AB=<s>` alternates the
  arms, CONTROL first, gated on game time in the cockpit as in take 323.
  Without it the arm is FIX always: that is the shipping form.
* **Scorer `csmfit`.**
  * PATCHED or REFUSED, and the phases.
  * Per arm: the cascade 0 X4 **drew**, taken from camuj as the largest sx
    among the orthographic blocks (the ones whose shadow inverse is never
    maintained), against the arm's prediction.
  * FAIL if fewer than half the readings sit within 1% (the arms did not
    differ), if it was asked and not patched, or if the phases never started.
* **Census:** 9 new cases (healthy, collapsed, refused, never patched, never
  started, not asked).
* **`tests/csmfit.cpp`, 27 checks.**
  * X4's formula against take 323's three boxes and the logged thresholds.
  * Divisors and coverage, including a non-square aspect.
  * The sites against the real binary.
  * The address the injector picks, which all four sites can reach.
  * The patch run for real: X4's own instruction bytes, placed on an
    executable page, return X4's values before the retarget and the private
    pair after it. The private pair changes live, and only the displacement
    changes. Refusals cover a target out of reach and sites on two pages.

**Dry run in X4's own process.** gdb started X4 with the injector preloaded
and `X4VR_CSM_COVER=0.663` and stopped at X4's entry point (0x9accb0), where
our constructor has run and X4's code has not. Results:

* The log said PATCHED.
* gdb decodes the four instructions as `cvtss2sd ...(%rip) # 0x3f0004 /
  0x3f0000 / 0x3f0000 / 0x3f0004`.
* The page 0x2095000 is mapped r-x again.
* The private page sits at 0x3f0000, rw, holding (1.0, 1.0).

The process was killed there: no window, no file opened.

### Issue 1: the map's right-click menu closes, and its options are hard to hit

Patola: *"I could not click the guidance menu option most of the time, and
sometime I right-clicked and the small menu disappeared in 2 seconds."*

**X4's rule, from its Lua.** `ego_interactmenu/menu_interactmenu.lua`,
`menu.onUpdate`, runs every 0.1 s. With a mouse (not a gamepad) it closes the
menu the moment `GetLocalMousePosition()` is more than `mouseOutRange = 100`
px outside the menu's frame. So when the menu vanished, X4's own pointer had
left it.

**What our side did in the map** (the longest session, 363462–363509 s):

* head-look idle ("HUD is now down — idle, mouse handed back"), no camera
  writes;
* evflow: `motion pushed 0.0 Hz` — no synthetic mouse motion;
* the layer drew the cursor at X4's pointer (ARM B, canvas off).

Nothing of ours is known to move the pointer there. Two candidates remain,
neither established:

* **(a) SteamVR's own window takes focus or the pointer.** It has a desktop
  window; WiVRn does not. The map had never been exercised under head-look
  write mode on WiVRn either (takes 321–325 did not open it).
* **(b) Something of ours that only shows in the map**, such as where the drawn
  cursor sits against where X4 hit-tests in a full-screen menu.

**Next: the discriminating case.** The same map action on WiVRn: open the map,
pick a place, right-click, choose "guidance". The injector does not log
window focus or mouse enter/leave events; add that before the take, so a
focus change answers (a) directly. Patola's recording is the other
instrument: what the headset showed while the menu closed.

### Issue 2: the mouse-steering line is anchored at the nose, the steering at the gaze

Patola: *"when we look up, down, to the sides, the effective center is where
our gaze is, so the mouse should be relative to that place ... maybe making
the 'center' accompany our gaze alongside the line should be considered? But
I'm afraid that it can break other elements of the interface."*

**X4's Lua confirms it exactly.** `ui/core/lua/crosshair handling.lua`,
`updateMouseSteeringLine()`, draws the line as a CHILD of the crosshair
element, the ship's nose. The line runs from that origin to
`GetLocalMousePosition()` × 10, the pointer's offset from the SCREEN centre.
X4 steers by that same screen-centre offset. With the camera forward the two
agree. With head-look, the nose sits at offset c on screen, and the line is
drawn translated by c from where the steering is measured. Its direction and
length are right; its anchor is wrong. In vanilla, free-look and mouse
steering never coexist, so X4 never had to reconcile them.

**Fix (Patola's suggestion, and it touches nothing else).** An override of
`updateMouseSteeringLine` in our extension draws the same segment translated
by −c: from the screen centre (gaze) to the pointer, in the crosshair's local
frame. Steering itself, hover and the cursor are untouched: X4 already steers
relative to the gaze, so this only makes the line tell the truth. c is the
projection of the ship's forward axis under the head-look rotation that the
injector writes. The Lua side needs it, through the planned FFI bridge (a
Lua `ffi.C` declaration resolving a symbol the injector exports) or a Lua API
that gives the crosshair's screen position, if one exists.

## Take 326's map menu, from the recording: our cursor mapping, not SteamVR

Patola's recording (`/jogos/videos/x4-foundations-vr-mod-voo-1.mp4`) is the
headset view, one eye, 1920×1080, 554.4 s. It is synced to the log by the
first map opening: video 169.0 s ↔ log 398.7 s, so **log = video + 363229.7
s** (±0.25 s). Frames stay in the scratchpad; X4's rendered output is never
committed.

**What it shows** (video 237.6–242 s = log 467.3–471.7 s, in the long map
session):

* The right-click menu ("Avarice V Dead End": Show Encyclopedia Entry /
  Actions / Start Guidance to Position) is open.
* From 239.2 s to 241.2 s the drawn cursor sits ON "Start Guidance to
  Position", and the row never highlights.
* The cursor's shape is X4's four-arrow **map-pan** cursor. X4 picks the shape
  from where IT thinks the pointer is, which was over the map, not the menu.
* `menu_interactmenu.lua` closes the menu when that pointer is >100 px
  outside it ("disappeared in 2 seconds").

**The mechanism was measured in take 311 and then undone without noticing.**

* Take 311: in the map and full-screen menus, X4 hit-tests in its UI, which
  the layer shows scaled by the canvas map (0.5252). The cursor must be drawn
  through that map there. Drawing it at the raw pointer puts it n/A from where
  X4 tests: "the error grows with distance from the centre".
* Take 314: in flight X4 picks the world at the raw pointer, so raw is right
  there.
* Take 315 and every take since shipped `X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS=0`, raw
  everywhere, and the map was not opened again until take 326.

The per-context choice take 314 named as open is the fix. **SteamVR is not
implicated.** The planned focus and enter/leave logging is not built: the
recording answered the question it was for.

**`X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS=auto`.**

* The injector polls X4's `IsFullscreenMenuDisplayed(true, NULL)` each tick
  on X4's main thread and publishes it in the shared channel (`fullscreen_menu`,
  share v4). The function is declared in X4's Lua cdefs. With anymenu true it
  tail-calls 0x117f7c0, which walks X4's static open-menu table (a std::map
  header at 0x3dfc200, never NULL, alive until main() returns).
* The layer draws the cursor through the canvas while it reads 1 and at the
  raw pointer otherwise.
* Both ends log their changes: `ui: full-screen menu UP/DOWN` and
  `cursor canvas: AUTO — ON/OFF`. Scorer `cursor-auto` counts both, and FAILs
  a menu the injector saw that never switched the layer. Census +5.

**Not covered: the cockpit right-click menu** (HUD up, no full-screen menu)
still draws raw. If it misbehaves like the map did, the Lua link (the
steering-line work) can report the interact menu's open/close.

   explain an up-left offset. He has a movie of it; the movie decides.

   X4 set no cursor of its own until the cockpit (first set at log 405930;
   "X4 built 26 cursor(s) and has not SET one" before). On the start screen it
   shows SDL's default system cursor, which our capture never sees, so the
   layer has no image to draw.
3. **"Head-look write ARMED" arrived at ~65% of the save's loading screen**
   (log 405888). Arming waits for the camera and X4's loaded look-around
   parameters, not for play. Harmless, but the notice misleads. It should
   wait for game time, as fieldab and csmfit do.
4. **Right-click on objects to the side gives a "slanted" (perspective) menu,
   and far to the side it "either doesn't work or does something invisible".**
   This is P327.4's unknown: the cockpit right-click menu is UI (canvas-scaled),
   while the cursor in flight is raw. The mismatch grows with distance from
   the centre, and X4 closes the menu once its pointer is 100 px out.
   `NotifyInteractMenuShown/Hidden` only dispatch a script event (0xa474b0,
   0xa473d0); there is no flag to poll. The menu's open state has to come from
   Lua. He does not mind the slant.

**Next, in order:**

* **The Lua link**: a Lua add-on in our extension, with Protected UI Mode
  served off by our config fork, calling into functions the injector exports
  (`ffi.C`). The injector already sees every chunk X4 loads through
  `luaL_loadbuffer`, but they may arrive as bytecode, so source patching is
  not the route. Through the link:
  * report the cockpit right-click menu, so the cursor uses the canvas while
    it is open;
  * measure, then fix, the steering line.
* **The start screen's default cursor**: draw X4's own arrow when X4 has set
  none.
* **ARMED waits for game time.**
* **The map-fit offset**, from his movie.

### The map cursor's fit, from Patola's movie (`/dados/x4-map-issue.mp4`)

The clip was recorded in the headset (the system overlay shows in its first and
last frames): 72.7 s, 1920×1080, with the map open from 5 s to 28 s.

* **The cursor leaves the map at the top.** At 27.0 s the drawn cursor, an
  arrow, sits at (883, 292), ~136 px above the panel's top edge (y≈428), over
  the cockpit window. X4 chose the arrow, not the map's circled-target
  cursor, so **X4 also placed its pointer outside the map there**. Drawn and
  hit-tested position may agree, and the question becomes where X4 lays the
  map out in our square window.
* **X4 letterboxes full-screen content in a square window.** Take 274's UI
  dumps (2816×2816, after the layer's 0.5252 scale) show the loading screen as
  a centred **16:9 band**: 52% of the width and 30% of the height
  (= 0.5252 × 9/16). The start screen's background fills the square. If the map
  is laid out in a band too, the pointer's full-window range overshoots it
  above and below.
* **A confound we serve ourselves:** the player's config has
  `<uiscale>0.6</uiscale>` (set for his 3400×1440 desktop), and our config
  fork passes it through to the 2816×2816 VR window unchanged.
* **Not explained:** Patola's "doesn't go all the way to the left or the
  bottom" is an asymmetry. A centred band explains none of it. It is
  recorded, not reasoned away.

**To measure, not guess:** the first job of the Lua link is to report X4's own
layout numbers: `Helper.viewWidth/viewHeight`, the UI scale, and the map
frame's rectangle in window pixels. A UI dump of the map goes beside them, and
the pointer's extents are already logged. The fix depends on the numbers. It
may be clamping the pointer to the content while a full-screen menu is up,
or serving a VR-appropriate uiscale.

## Built for take 328: start-screen cursor, ARMED timing, map-edge and Lua measurements

  32×32; hotspot (7,8) six times, (0,0) once, the rest centred or offset) and
  sets none until the cockpit. The start screen shows SDL's default system
  arrow, never captured. Now X4's first-built cursor (#0, 32×32 hot (7,8))
  is published as soon as it is built and stands in until X4's first own

* **ARMED notice.** Arming is unchanged: it still happens when the camera and

* **The map's edges, measured by X4.** Every cursor change inside a
  full-screen menu (up to 400) logs the pointer position. X4 switches shape

* **Lua reconnaissance** (`X4VR_LUA=1`). Each chunk logs its Lua state pointer

* Census +6 (210).

## Decisions after take 328 (Patola, 2026-10-12), and the plan

**Steering target:** *"B looks like a better option, but A also feels
interesting, so yes, I want a toggle to switch between the two behaviors if
that's easy to do, maybe F8 or apostrophe?"*

* **B (default): the cursor where you look, the line fixed.** Cursor, hover
  and steering are unchanged. X4's `updateMouseSteeringLine` (in
  `ui/core/lua/crosshair handling.lua`) is overridden to draw the same segment
  translated by −c, so it starts at the screen centre (the gaze) instead of
  the crosshair (the nose). c is the nose's screen offset under head-look.
* **A: the target fixed to the cockpit while steering.** The layer draws the
  cursor at nose + offset while X4 reports mouse steering active. X4's own
  line then ends on it, and steering is in ship axes. Cost: hover and
  click-select stay at the screen-fixed pointer, so they are off by the head
  angle while steering. Weapons are unaffected (his `forceshootatcursor` is
  false).
* **The toggle:** a key the injector intercepts and swallows: F8 or
  apostrophe, whichever his inputmap leaves free. It switches A/B live and
  sends a notice.

**The map's margins are a blocker, not cosmetic:** *"it makes some important
sections of the map (or whatever info appears on this quad) unreachable ...
there are many left menus on X4's map screen and other screens that will be
non-functional with this shift/limitation."* The measured pointer reach is the
whole window, so an unreachable menu means some UI is DISPLAYED outside where
the pointer can map to.

* **Leading hypothesis (#82's two populations):** not every UI element goes
  through the 0.5252 UI scale (perspective-drawn UI does; orthographic
  "markers" may not). Elements drawn unscaled would appear at up to ±1.0 of
  the eye, while the canvas-mapped pointer reaches ±0.5252.
* **Alternatively,** X4's layout at uiscale 0.6 places the left menus beyond
  the window.
* **To measure:**
  * a UI dump of the map screen (`X4VR_UI_DUMP`), with the left menus' pixel
    positions compared against the window and the canvas reach;
  * Patola naming which menus he cannot reach.

**Order of work:**

1. Measure from Patola's steering recording (below): where the crosshair and
   the line land in the headset against the drawn cursor, with the head
   straight and turned. That decides whether the 0.5252 UI scale also
   shortens the line, which both A and B must account for.
2. The map's unreachable menus: dump, measure, fix (a pointer mapping that
   covers everything displayed, or a layout X4 keeps inside the window).
3. A/B steering with the toggle: injector Lua injection into the crosshair
   state for B, layer cursor placement for A, and the key.
4. Small items already built: start-screen stand-in #5, renamed watcher
   notice. They ride in the next take.

## Take 328B — the circles and the map's unreachable menus, read (2026-10-15)

Material:
* **The recording** `/dados/x4-circles.mp4`: the headset view, one eye,
  1920×1080 at 90 fps, 352.5 s. Cockpit from 01:43. Steering circles with the
  head centred (02:16), turned left (02:28), right (02:44) and up (02:54). The
  map from 03:04, swept along its limits through the property list,
  Encyclopedia, Diplomacy, Empire Overview and Tutorials until 05:40.
* **The log** `/tmp/x4vr-take328b.log`: take 328's command line run again as
  X4VR_TAKE=328B. `score_run.py`: PASS.

Patola: *"I was wrong, they are mostly reachable. But I go through several
menus and I show the regions that are unreachable. It is actually not a
straight left margin compared to the map, it's a mostly vertical but slightly
diagonal limit, which is close to the origin at the top but far from it at the
bottom."*

### The map: X4's camera is frozen at the head's angle

**Cause.** X4 draws its UI on a plane fixed to the cockpit, seen through the
player camera at the UI field (tan 0.75). It hit-tests the pointer through the
same projection. The pointer is confined to the window, which is that camera's
view. With the camera turned, the UI plane is keystoned and shifted inside the
window, and part of it falls outside where the pointer can go.

Why the camera is turned:
* X4's look follower recentres the camera when look-around ends. Take 311,
  the MOUSELOOK actuator: every one of its 14 HUD-down periods settled at
  0,0 within a fraction of a second.
* `x4vrmod_headlook` sets `anglespeed` 0 so a written head angle STAYS (take
  321). That also stopped the recentring.
* So since X4VR_HEADLOOK_WRITE, every menu opened at the head's angle and
  stayed there:
  * 328B: −1.99°, +6.37° for all 157 s of map and sub-menus (8144 readings).
  * 328: −2.87°, +2.89°.
  * 327: a different angle at every opening, pitch 5.4–14.4°, yaw −2.9 to
    +1.4°. That is why the limits seemed to move between sessions.

**The model, and X4's own hit-testing reproduced from the log alone.** The
model is a flat UI plane filling the unrotated view at tan 0.75, seen by a
camera rotated by X4's logged angle; in GetCameraRotation's convention both
signs flip. Each cursor-shape change X4 logged was mapped into UI coordinates
and compared with X4's layout from its own Lua (`helper.lua`: `frameBorder`
18, `sidebarWidth` 40 × `uiScale` 1, right bar at `viewWidth − 40 − 18`).
* 328B, arrow (#5) at pointer (2643, 557) → UI x **2816.0**: the UI's right
  edge, to the pixel.
* 328B, (2625, 562) #5 → 2795.5, inside the right bar [2758, 2798].
  (2632, 566) #12 → 2803, the 18-px frame border where the map shows.
* 328B, the top-left corner flips land within ~10 UI px of (0, 0).
* 328, an independent angle: the model puts the top edge at window y 90–189,
  and take 328 measured ~184. The flip at (2534, 182) → UI y −3.5. The flip
  at (2664, 1072) → UI x 2819.

**What was out of reach in 328B: 13.6% of X4's UI.**
* A left wedge, from UI x ≈ 5 at the top (UI y 150) to x ≈ 195 at the
  window's bottom: Patola's "close to the origin at the top, far at the
  bottom".
* The bottom band, UI y > ~2490–2540, across the full width.
* Above and to the right, the pointer could go BEYOND the UI. That is take
  327's *"it goes a bit after the map to the left and up"*.
* All of 328B's menus shared the one frozen angle, so every screen he showed
  had the same wedge and band.

**The video agrees.**
* With the pointer at x = 0 (log), the drawn arrow sits ~37–47 video px
  inside the left edge of X4's view, more at the bottom.
* At 192.2 s X4 shows the "Object List" tooltip exactly where the drawn
  cursor overlaps the sidebar's second icon. So X4's hit-test follows the
  drawing, and the cursor and the UI share one map.

**A second defect, the same cause.** During menus the layer declared an
identity pose (`poselag: declared=0,0 valid=0`), while X4 rendered from
−1.99°, 6.37°. So the whole menu frame was displayed rotated by ~6.6°.

**Wrong turns, recorded:**
* Take 328's scoring said *"X4 lays the map out in a box ... with uneven
  margins (top ~184, right ~136)"*. Wrong: the margins were the frozen
  camera.
* The persisted leading hypothesis (#82's two populations, some UI unscaled)
  is **refuted**. The canvas is a diagonal scale-plus-shift
  (`make_canvas_k`). The cursor applies the same `CanvasNdc`. X4's hit-test
  agrees with the drawing.
* The uiscale-0.6 alternative is **refuted**. X4's layout at uiScale 1
  matches the hit-test boundaries.
* The planned UI dump was not needed: the log reproduced X4's hit-testing.
* Video handling:
  * `ffmpeg -ss … -t … out_%03d.png` without `-fps_mode passthrough`
    duplicated frames (a 0.6 s strip "frozen").
  * Syncing on the map's first frame lags cursor events by ~0.5 s (the
    holomap's first render). Sync on cursor-shape changes instead.
* A `pkill -f` on the census script killed its own shell (the standing
  self-match rule, broken again).

### The steering circles, measured

In each circle: the nose (crosshair), the end of X4's steering line, and our
ring cursor (X4's #20/#24, drawn at the raw pointer).

    circle (frame)         ring cursor     line end observed   G + 0.5252 (ring − G)   residual
    centre 02:16 (141 s)   (975, 220)      (966, 310)          (966.9, 309.3)          1.2 px
    left   02:28 (152 s)   (934, 517)      (947, 464)          (945.4, 465.2)          2.0 px
    right  02:44 (165 s)   (934, 486.7)    (945.7, 449.3)      (945.4, 449.3)          0.3 px  (out of sample)
    up     02:54 (177 s)   (1069, 288)     (1017, 348)         (1016.3, 345.0)         3.1 px  (out of sample)

G = (958, 408) was fitted on the centre and left circles. It is the eye's
centre, the gaze; this recording's crop puts it 133 px above the frame centre.

**So:**
* X4's line starts at the nose, which is fixed to the cockpit.
* It ends at the pointer's position on the HUD plane: the gaze plus 0.5252 ×
  the pointer's offset. This is `GetLocalMousePosition()`, read in
  `updateMouseSteeringLine`.
* Our ring cursor is drawn at the raw pointer, where X4 picks the WORLD
  (take 314). That is 1.904× farther from the gaze than the line's end.
* X4 steers by the pointer's offset from the gaze (Patola: *"the effective
  center is where our gaze is"*).

For the A/B design:
* **B:** to run from the gaze to the drawn ring, X4's segment must be
  translated by −c AND lengthened by 1/0.5252. c is the nose's offset from
  the gaze on the HUD plane.
* **A:** the ring placed relative to the nose must use the same 0.5252
  relation, or the line and the ring disagree by the same factor.
* c is the camera's axis meeting the HUD plane: the projection the map fix
  rests on, validated above against X4's own hit-testing.

### The fix: X4VR_HEADLOOK_MENU_CENTRE (built, default ON with X4VR_HEADLOOK_WRITE)

* **What it does.** While the HUD is down in the cockpit, the injector writes
  X4's camera to 0,0 every tick. It is the follower's spring-back that
  `anglespeed` 0 took away.
* **How.** Through the same guarded write as head-look:
  * the same `camwrite_ready` (sites, camera mode 0, X4's parameters, base
    identity);
  * the same `process_vm_writev`.

  It is not a new patch of X4.
* **What it leaves alone.**
  * `steering` stays false, so nothing is declared as head motion.
  * Its writes are counted apart from the head's.
* **Logging.** Once per period: `headlook: HUD down in the cockpit — X4's
  camera CENTRED from yaw Y pitch P to 0,0`. The write report gains `menu
  centring N period(s) M write(s)`.
* **Bisect.** `X4VR_HEADLOOK_MENU_CENTRE=0` restores 328B: the camera stays
  where the head was.
* **Not covered.** Full-screen menus that switch the view to external
  (327 ×2, 328B's last 13 s, at +0.96, +16.03: 27.5% of the UI out of
  reach). The centring acts only while `x4_cockpit_view()` holds, so nothing
  is written there. `menucam` reports them; whether X4 draws those menus
  through the player camera is unmeasured.

**Scorer: `menucam`** (census: frozen, centred, asked-but-frozen = FAIL,
switched off = no FAIL, silent without write-mode arming). For each HUD-down
period after arming it reports:
* X4's settled camera angle;
* the view;
* the model's share of X4's UI outside the window.

It FAILs a run that asked for the centring (write mode, not switched off, a
build whose write report carries the field) if a cockpit period stays
off-centre. On 328B it reports `-1.99,+6.37 OFF-CENTRE 13.6%`, with no FAIL,
since that build had no centring.

Protocol (no timed phases; configuration 1, real mouse and keyboard;
WiVRn):
1. Start WiVRn and run the line. Load the save. Wait for the "head-look
   write ARMED" notification.
2. Turn the head clearly away from straight ahead (~20–30° to one side and
   a little up or down) and press M.
3. With the map open, sweep the cursor along all four edges. Go into the
   left menus as in 328B, especially their lower parts.
4. Close the map, fly a few seconds, then open it again with the head
   turned the other way. Repeat the sweep.
5. Quit.

Cost: ~5 minutes. No extra instrumentation. One memory write per tick while
a menu is up. A short recording of one sweep is welcome but not required:
the scorer measures the camera, and his report judges reachability.

went way further to the left and up and stopped way before the right and
lower corners."*

`score_run.py`: PASS. No X4 or gamescope core in the journal.

* **P329.1 HELD for the map.** Both cockpit menu periods were CENTRED (0.0%
  out of reach): from head yaw **+30.84** (left) and **−53.55** (right), both
  at pitch ~+9.
* **P329.2 HELD.** Everything was reachable and the cursor stayed inside the
  quad, in both head directions.
* **P329.4 HELD.** `hwrite` tracking: yaw p90 3.58°, pitch p90 4.76°. Head-look
  resumed after each map.
* **P329.5 HELD.** csmfit 26/26 FIX; cursor-auto 13/13; the start-screen
  arrow #5 was shown.
* **NEW, the ESC menu: the same defect, and a mislabel of mine hid it.**
  * ESC at 207683.11: `view is now external/floating — idle`, a full-screen
    menu UP, and the HUD down.
  * X4's camera stayed at **+2.17, +9.24** for the whole 22 s menu. That is
    the head's angle when ESC was pressed, and 18.2% of X4's UI was out of
    reach.
  * The model's direction matches his report exactly: the UI is shifted down
    and right, so the cursor overshoots left and up and falls short right and
    down.
  * **Why the centring did not act.** `x4_cockpit_view()` returns false when
    `IsGamePaused()` is true, and **the ESC menu pauses** (take 146 had
    written this down). The single log label "external/floating" covered
    external, floating AND paused, so a paused cockpit read as "not the
    cockpit", and the centring is gated on the cockpit.
  * It fired at 207705.6, when the view flipped back to "the cockpit"
    during the quit itself.
  * Take 328B's last period (+0.96, +16.03, "external/floating", 13 s)
    and 327's two "external" periods were most likely the same ESC menu.

**The fix:**
* `x4_view()` names which predicate said "not the cockpit": cockpit,
  external, floating, PAUSED. The log line now says which.
* The centring acts in the cockpit OR paused with the HUD down (the cockpit's
  camera either way).
* Its CENTRED line says `(PAUSED)` when it centred under the pause.
* `menucam` reads the new labels, judges PAUSED periods like cockpit ones,
  and NOTEs the pre-329 label.

**The open question the take must answer.** Does X4 apply a camera write
while paused?
* If it does not rebuild the view during a pause, the write lands in the
  free-look matrix but the menu stays where it was drawn.
* GetCameraRotation (`x4=`, `camstamp`) reads the state we write, not the
  view X4 rendered, so the log cannot tell those apart. His eye on the ESC
  menu decides.
* The MOUSELOOK-era logs that could have answered it (take 311's pauses,
  under X4's own follower) are gone: `/tmp` was cleaned by age.

**Lost with them: the scorer suites' bases.** `/tmp/x4vr-take306.log`
(census), `x4vr-take303.log` (pace) and `x4vr-take294.log` (rfab) were all
cleaned out of `/tmp`. Each suite then printed SKIP and **exited 0**: suites
that pass by testing nothing, a guard that cannot fail.
* The base is now **committed**: `tests/data/census-base.log`, 313 lines,
  built by `tests/make-census-base.sh` from a real take's log:
  * the first 200 lines, for the render-pass inventory;
  * its first 20 live camera reads;
  * its periodic `vr copy`/`vr summary` series;
  * take 303's run line, which asks for none of the later features;
  * those features' own start-up lines removed (content fork, csmfit, cursor
    stand-in, roll, `vr pace`);
  * the profile ID scrubbed.
* The three suites default to it (`X4VR_CENSUS_BASE` overrides). A missing
  base now FAILs instead of SKIPping.
* Results: census **224/224**, pace 21/21, rfab 13/13.

**And a scorer bug that the small base exposed.** `menucam` printed
`t0+…` with the perf block's `t0`, which exists only when a run logged perf
windows. On a short log it raised UnboundLocalError, and every block after
`menucam` was lost. It now falls back to the log's first timestamp.
Two of the census's expected strings followed the verdicts' new wording ("…
cockpit or ESC-pause period(s)").

Protocol (no timed phases; configuration 1, real mouse and keyboard;
WiVRn):
1. Start WiVRn and run the line. Load the save. Wait for the "head-look
   write ARMED" notification.
2. Open the map once with the head turned and check it is still fitted.
   Close it.
3. Turn the head clearly to one side (~30°, a little up or down) and press
   ESC. Sweep the cursor along all four edges of the ESC menu and into its
   corners. Press ESC again to resume.
4. Fly a few seconds. Turn the head to the other side and do step 3 again.
5. Quit through the ESC menu.

Cost: ~5 minutes. No recording needed: the question is categorical, fitted or
not, judged within the run.

## The steering target, A/B with a toggle — built (2026-10-26)

Patola, after take 328: B (the default) and A, switched live by a key.
Geometry from take 328B's circles: X4's line runs from the nose to gaze +
0.5252 × (the pointer's offset), and our ring sits at the raw pointer. So the
line can neither start where steering is measured from nor end on the ring.

**The design: X4's line off, ours drawn in eye space.** No Lua injection.
* **Hiding X4's line.** X4 has an option for it: `IsMouseSteeringLineEnabled`
  and `SetMouseSteeringLine`, config tag `mousesteeringline`, default true.
  Patola's config omits it.
  * With `X4VR_STEER` set, the config fork serves it as `false`, inserting
    the tag (`set_or_insert_tag`, the one exception to "never invent a
    tag").
  * X4 saves settings while it runs, so the replaced value goes into a
    sidecar (`config-x4vrmod-mousesteeringline.was`). A later run without
    `X4VR_STEER` puts it back and deletes the sidecar. Patola's own
    config.xml is never touched.
* **When to draw: X4's own condition, read rather than called.**
  * `ShouldShowMouseSteeringHelperLine` (0xa45cb0) is
    `option && (in[0x9f36] || in[0x9f37]) && in[0x9f42] && (!in[0x9f39] ||
    in[0xa010])`, with `in` = *0x3daaaf8.
  * That is the object `IsMouseSteeringActive` (0xa45940) reads WITH NO NULL
    CHECK. So the injector reads those five bytes through process_vm_readv
    after verifying 16 code sites, plus the cockpit view with the HUD up (the
    Lua side's crosshairActive).
  * A changed build refuses, and then X4's own line is left alone too.
* **Where to draw: the layer, in the eye image, both eyes alike (the target
  is at infinity).**
  * **B (`X4VR_STEER=b`):** the ring stays at the raw pointer, where X4
    picks. The line runs from the eye's centre, which is X4's screen centre
    and the reference X4 steers from, to the ring.
  * **A (`a`):** the ring is drawn at the nose plus the same offset, and the
    line from the nose to it. The nose is the cockpit's forward axis,
    rotated by X4's camera as stamped at the frame's first render pass,
    projected at the rendered field. That is
    `(sin yaw, −cos yaw sin pitch, cos yaw cos pitch)`, which
    `tests/steer.cpp` checks equals `rows_for`'s convention over 35 poses.
    A frame where the nose is behind or off the eye falls back to B, so a
    cursor stays.
  * The line copies X4's: white at alpha 12% (`white_alpha_12`; measured
    ~0.10 in the 328B recording), 2 px plus 1 px feathers, starting 16 px
    out as X4 leaves 30 crosshair units. The cursor is drawn over its end.
* **The toggle: apostrophe** (SDL scancode 52, a physical key).
  * It is unbound in all six of Patola's input maps. F8 is X4's compass slot
    2, its debug key and the cinematic letterbox.
  * It is plain only: Shift/Ctrl/Alt/GUI/AltGr chords pass through. It acts
    only in the cockpit with the HUD up; anywhere else it is X4's.
  * It is removed from what `SDL_PeepEvents` hands X4, on peek and get, and
    acts on the get. `SDL_WaitEvent` gets scancode 0.
  * Each switch logs `milestone: steering target A|B`, which the watcher
    relays as a notification.

**Tests (pass):**
* `tests/steer.cpp` (32 checks): the knob; the predicate's truth table; the
  16 sites against the real binary, with a flipped byte that must refuse; the
  option string; the nose; B/A/fallback/gap geometry; the line quad; the
  config insert/replace/restore.
* `tests/run-cursor.sh` (7 GPU runs, under validation):
  * the five existing ones, unchanged by the generalised quad shader
    (origin plus two edge vectors; solid when u0 < 0);
  * two steering runs. In each, the midpoint pixel is X4's 31/255, 4 px
    beside the line and inside the gap are untouched, and the cursor is
    drawn OVER the line (green 15, where the line on top would read 31). In
    A the ring moves by the nose's offset.
* Census 236/236, with 9 `steer` cases.

**Scorer `steer`.**
* It reports: the site check; whether X4's line was hidden; how often X4
  would have shown its line; the toggles in order; the frames drawn per mode,
  with lines and A-to-B fallbacks.
* It FAILs:
  * a refusal;
  * a line not hidden;
  * X4 showing its line while the layer never drew;
  * A chosen and never drawn.

**Known limit:** an apostrophe typed into a text field that X4 opens in the
cockpit with the HUD up would toggle instead of typing. No such field is in
use.

Material:

Patola also: *"we still have that issue of the mouse starting way top/left,
so it automatically steers the ship this way and I spend some time centering
it."* The map and menus *"worked perfectly, including the corners."*

`score_run.py`: PASS.
* **P331.1 HELD.**
  * 16/16 sites matched, X4's own line was hidden through the fork, and the
    overlay started in B.
  * X4's line condition was ON 3 times. One apostrophe press: to A.
  * The layer drew B in 7056 frames and A in 3399, with a line in 10384.
* **P331.2 HELD (the primary), measured on the recording.**
  * In every B frame examined, the line extended backwards meets ONE fixed
    point, about (802, 692) of this recording, and ends on the ring. That
    covers the head straight (02:13 down, 02:19 right), looking right (02:34,
    02:37) and up (02:43, 02:46), from all sides.
  * That point is the eye's centre, X4's steering reference. With the head
    straight it sits about 60 px above the nose crosshair: Patola's usual
    head pitch of a few degrees up.
* **P331.3 HELD, with one defect.**
  * In A the line starts at the nose crosshair. Straight ahead it runs down
    to the ring; looking left it runs from the crosshair, at the right of the
    view, to the ring beside it. The ring rides with the cockpit.
  * **Defect:** looking right, the ring left the headset's view, and the
    scorer counted **0** fallbacks to B. The fallback tested the nose
    against the RENDERED eye (±55°), but the headset shows less: the runtime
    reports eye0 l=−54 r=40 u=44 d=−55, eye1 mirrored, so both eyes see only
    ±40° horizontally and 44° up. The nose and ring were in the render and
    out of sight.
* **P331.4 HELD.**
  * menucam: 3/3 centred, two of them PAUSED.
  * Tracking yaw p90 1.62°, pitch p90 1.02°; csmfit 47/47.
* **The top-left start, explained.**
  * When mouse steering engaged (Shift+Space, 274956.22), X4 set its cockpit
    cursor with the pointer at **(125, 62)** of the 2816-px window, and the
    ship steered hard up-left.
  * X4 never centres the pointer. Its only `SDL_WarpMouseInWindow` call
    (0xcefcd9) reads the pointer, adds a delta, clamps and warps: a nudge,
    not a centring.
  * In the headset the pointer sits wherever the load left it.

**Fixes, built:**
* **A's fallback tests the RING against what both eyes show.**
  `steer::binocular_box` maps the runtime's per-eye angles into the eye,
  published by the layer when it latches them (`steer: both eyes show x … y
  …`). A frame whose ring (nose + offset) falls outside, or whose nose is
  behind, is drawn as B.
* **The pointer recentres when mouse steering engages.**
  * The trigger is the steering bytes (0x9f36/0x9f37) going 0→1 in the
    cockpit with the HUD up, or the cockpit/HUD returning while they are
    set. Not the full line predicate, whose other flags are not known to be
    steady in flight.
  * The pointer is warped to the centre of X4's window through our own
    `SDL_WarpMouseInWindow`, so it is folded exactly like one of X4's.
  * Logged as `steer: mouse steering engaged — pointer recentred from x,y`.
    X4's own warps are now logged too (the first 20).
* **Scorer.**
  * `steer` reads both fallback wordings (take 331's "nose off the eye", now
    "ring out of sight"), reports the box, and counts recentres with their
    origin.
  * Census 239/239; tests/steer.cpp gained the box from take 331's numbers
    and the out-of-sight fallback; GPU 7/7.

   turn.
3. Fly a circle with the pointer in B.
4. Disengage, move the mouse to a corner, and engage again. The ship should
   start straight.
5. Open and close the map with steering on. The ship should start straight
   again.
6. Press apostrophe for A. Look far right (as at 331's 03:32) and far left:
   the ring should stay visible.
7. Apostrophe back to B, then quit.

Cost: ~5–10 minutes. No recording needed (each check is see-it-or-not), but
one is welcome.

## Roadmap after take 333 (Patola, 2026-10-27)

**Next, Patola to choose: (1) mouse controls in walking mode, or (2) aiming
gimbaled weapons.**
* **Gimbaled weapons** aim independently at a far point in front of the ship,
  where the cursor points. The logistics are hard: testing needs ships with
  each weapon type, and changing ships needs walking, which does not work
  yet.
* **A's cost, which (2) runs straight into:** X4 picks and aims at the RAW
  pointer (gaze + offset), while A draws the ring at nose + offset. So with
  the head turned, gimbals would aim where the ring is NOT.
  * Aiming work must either move X4's aim point to the ring's direction, or
    show where X4 actually aims.
  * Same family: the cockpit right-click interact menu on objects far to the
    side (slanted, or closing); it is still drawn raw.
* My recommendation: (1) walking first. It unblocks the ship-switching (2)
  needs to test both weapon types, and walking already has known edges: the
  HUD is head-locked only on foot, and gamescope's `--force-grab-cursor`
  fix for the view pinned to the floor.

**Later, when refining X4's many views (not now):**
* **Numpad view rotation in third-person (chase) and target view.** Those
  keys turn the view there and do nothing now, because head-look took the
  numpad. They might be restored per view (X4 reports external/floating, see
  `x4_view()`), by passing the keys through or driving that view's camera.
  Station construction may use the numpad the same way: check.
* **Immersive third-person and target views.** They show as a rectangle, not
  the whole scene; the full field, if feasible.
* **Menus that switch to the external view are not centred**
  (X4VR_HEADLOOK_MENU_CENTRE acts in the cockpit and the ESC pause only).

## Walking mode, step 1: what X4's camera does out of the seat (P334)

Patola, 2026-10-27: *"go ahead with walking mode first"*.

**What is known, from the code and the record (no on-foot run since take 321):**
* Head-look's write refuses any camera mode but 0 (`camwrite_ready`: "the
  camera is in mode N, not the cockpit's 0"), so on foot it writes nothing.
  `steering` is then false and the layer declares identity: the picture is a
  window fixed in front of the play space (take 116's "a quad put at my
  front"). That is what "walking doesn't work" is, as far as the code says.
  None of takes 329-333 left the seat; older logs are gone from /tmp.
* 0x1933d00 dispatches on camera+0x880: **0** the cockpit (free-look in the
  matrix, read 2026-10-02); **1** jumps straight to the compose -- NO angle
  update at all, the stored transform is only re-based and written back;
  **2/3** and **4** orbit with the mouse on the external parameters
  (+0x6ac/+0x6b0 limits, +0x6b8/+0x6bc speeds); >4 elsewhere. Which one
  walking uses is not decidable statically; `<playercamera>` has no
  first-person look parameters at all.
* X4's UI receives a `gameplanchange` event naming `cockpit`, `external`,
  `firstperson` and `externalfirstperson`; on `firstperson` the HUD drops the
  radar and `firstperson_crosshair` takes over. That is Lua-side only.
* Picking on foot goes through the frame centre (the crosshair): X4 hides
  the pointer there (docs/frame-analysis.md, "The three cursor quirks are one
  bug", quirk 3).

**The target (Patola's spec where he gave one, mine where marked):**
the head turns the view freely on foot; the mouse keeps turning the body as
X4 does (*mine*); the minimal HUD is head-locked on foot (Patola,
2026-09-02: *"When in walking mode it makes sense for the minimal HUD to stay
headlocked"*); X4 picks through the frame centre, so with the view on the
head the pick follows the gaze (*mine, to confirm*).

**Built: `X4VR_FOOTLOG=1`** (`injector/x4vr_foot.hpp`, read only). Every
50 ms on X4's thread: the camera, its mode, its attached object (+0x780) and
that object's vtable, `GetPlayerControlledShipID`/`GetPlayerOccupiedShipID`
(declared in X4's Lua as `UniverseID f(void)`; both test their global -- the
guard checker now tells a `lea` from a read and has controls for both),
`GetCameraRotation`, the camera's local (+0x5a0..) and base (+0x6f0..)
transforms, the head, and the player's own mouse motion summed where X4
receives it. A `foot: regime` line on every change of camera / mode /
attached / piloting / occupied; a `foot: window` line each second with the
net and travel of yaw and pitch per source, any rotation (geodesic, so a roll
is not missed) and the translation's displacement. Milestones: "out of the
seat" (only after the player has piloted, so the load screen cannot fire it)
and "has enough" (60 s off the seat, mouse both ways, head turned). Scorer
block `foot`: per regime, which source FOLLOWS the mouse (correlation over
mouse-only windows, with the gain's sign) and which follows the head
(head-only windows); "NOTHING we read" is a verdict it can give. Tests:
tests/foot.cpp (angles against rows_for, the seam, a roll, a camera change,
the line); its `--emit` feeds the census suite the real formatter's output
(249 cases).

**Predictions, before the take:**
* **P334.1** out of the seat the camera reports a mode other than 0 -- my
  guess **1**, the path with no angle update -- with another attached object
  (the character), `piloting 0` and `occupied 1` inside the ship; back in the
  seat, mode 0 and `piloting 1` again. Refutation: mode 0 on foot, which
  would make the refusal not the reason nothing follows the head.
* **P334.2** on foot **the head turns nothing** (head-only windows: no source
  follows), and the log carries "REFUSED — the camera is in mode N". In the
  headset: a fixed window in front, black past its edge when the head turns.
  Refutation: something follows the head -- then something already carries
  it and the census names it.
* **P334.3** the mouse on foot: **its X turns nothing we read** (the body
  turns, in the attached object), **its Y turns the local matrix's pitch**
  and GetCameraRotation's. Medium confidence. Refutation: local yaw follows
  mouse X -- the walking view then lives in the camera's own matrix and the
  cockpit's write route applies almost as is; or nothing follows either axis
  -- both live in the character.
* **P334.4** the control: seated, head-only windows show the local matrix
  following the head (head-look's own write), and the cockpit pointer moves
  no matrix. Relative mouse is ON off the seat (X4's mouse-look) and off in
  the cockpit.
* **P334.5** nothing else changes -- the census writes nothing: menus
  centred, steering A, csmfit, tracking as in 333; scorer PASS.

**Take 334's line** = the shipping line (take 333's, `X4VR_STEER=a`) plus `X4VR_FOOTLOG=1`; nothing else differs. WiVRn, configuration 1.

## Take 334 — SCORED: on foot the camera is still mode 0, the write armed there, and it zeroed the mouse

PASS (no regression: menus centred 3/3, steering A drawn 3416 frames,
pointer recentred 2/2, the write armed). Patola went to a station, stood up,
waited for the notice, tried the mouse: *"It didn't turn with the mouse."*
Out of the ship the arrow keys turned him, *"but instead of my camera
turning and looking around, the quad where the scene is rotated from my
view"*; turning the head, *"it was the quad that was going out of view"*.

    regimes   seated: mode 0, piloting 1 occupied 1
              stood up: mode 0, piloting 0 occupied 0 -- SAME camera, SAME
              attached object (vtable 0x3b5f7a0), relative mouse ON
    off seat  92 s, 89 windows; GetCameraRotation 0,0 except one 9-s burst
              (-15, -34, +74, 11, -6, then parked at 3.99 until he sat);
              pitch 0 throughout; it ignored the head (r 0.00, 29 windows)

* **P334.1 REFUTED.** No mode change: walking keeps the cockpit's camera in
  mode 0, attached to the same object. So `camwrite_ready` passed on foot
  and head-look WROTE there all along -- and nothing followed: GetCameraRotation
  never moved with the head, and Patola saw no turn. On foot X4 does not
  render through the cockpit's free-look matrix, though it is mode 0.
* **The mouse: our defect, not X4's.** Writing on foot made `steering` true,
  and the event walk zeroes the player's relative mouse while steering (the
  rule from the MOUSELOOK actuator, where the mouse fought the servo). So X4
  received no mouse motion on foot. **P334.3 was not tested at all.**
* **The swinging quad, also ours.** `steering` true means the layer declares
  X4's rendered rotation (atdraw = GetCameraRotation); it moved during the
  arrow-key burst, so the picture was placed where X4 claimed to look.
* **P334.2 HELD in substance** (nothing X4 renders follows the head), for a
  different reason than predicted (not a refusal: a write that reaches
  nothing).

**Two wrong turns in the instrument, recorded:**
* The census summed the player's mouse BEFORE head-look zeroed it, credited
  X4 with 2851 counts it never received, and its verdict said *"the mouse
  turns NOTHING we read (the walking view lives elsewhere — the attached
  object)"*. A verdict about X4 built on an input that never reached X4
  ([[test-the-fix-where-it-can-act]]: the quantity was zero where it acted).
* It sampled after head-look's write in the same pump, so "local yaw/pitch
  FOLLOWS the head (r 1.00, slope 1.000)" was our own write read back
  ([[a-watcher-must-not-observe-itself]]).
Both fixed: it counts what X4 receives (and what was dropped), samples
before the write and says so in its banner; the scorer refuses a mouse
verdict when motion was dropped or counted the old way, and marks the local
column of a pre-335 census as our own write. Census suite +4.

**Fixed (P335):** in write mode head-look writes only **in the pilot seat**
(`GetPlayerControlledShipID != 0`: 1 seated, docked included; 0 from the
moment he stands, take 334). Off the seat nothing is written, MENU_CENTRE
included, `steering` is false, so (a) the mouse is no longer zeroed -- the
cockpit's handling is byte for byte unchanged -- and (b) the layer declares
identity: a window fixed in front, the scene turning inside it. Logged once
per transition ("out of the pilot seat — the write stands down" / "in the
pilot seat — the write may act"); the scorer FAILs a write-mode census that
saw the player off the seat without a stand-down.

## B, read statically: on foot X4 SKIPS the camera's own rotation (0x1929f70)

No run; X4 9.00. 0x1929f70(camera, &out, ref, time) is the per-frame
evaluation every camera snapshot goes through (take 316's hop 1). Mode 0:

1. `out` = the attached object's (+0x780) transform at `time` (0x18a0090).
2. The controller at camera+0x18; NULL -> return with `out` as it is.
3. If the attached object is the PLAYER (root+0x238, the object GetPlayerID
   reads) or the camera is the player's (root+0x3e8): `0x1de5df0()` -- the
   player's component chain from player+0x200, the first element of type
   0x16 -- and, if there is one, `0x1628210()`; **if that returns true,
   RETURN at 0x192a2f3 (`jne 192a216`): neither the controller nor the
   camera's own transform (+0x5a0..+0x5d0, the free-look) is composed.**
4. Otherwise compose the controller (vt+0x138) and then +0x5a0..+0x5d0.

`0x1628210()` takes no argument: with the player camera attached to the
player, true when the controller's chain at +0x58 has an element of type 6
(0x1de5eb0); else a compare of player+0x6aa8 with the global 0x3daa6f0
(and a byte at 0x3dab2dd on one path). The type numbers are not named
anywhere we have read.

**This fits takes 334/335 exactly:** the attached object is the same seated
and standing (it is the player, carried into the cockpit), the mode stays 0,
and our write to +0x5b0 never reached GetCameraRotation on foot -- the
branch drops it. On foot X4's view is the player object's own transform, so
GetCameraRotation follows the mouse and arrows (they turn the player).
(Not yet observed: which of step 2's NULL controller or step 3's branch it
is on foot; a read-only check of camera+0x18 and the predicate's data inputs
separates them.)

**What B needs, then:** the camera's own rotation composed on foot too --
the branch at 0x192a2f3 not taken -- and head-look's write active there.
X4's walking view (the player: mouse/arrow yaw, X4's pitch) times our head
rotation, exactly the cockpit's arrangement with the player in place of the
seat. That is a **code patch** (two bytes, in memory, verified first,
reverted at exit like X4VR_CSM_COVER's), and by the standing rule it is
Patola's decision. The data-only alternative is A (no patch: turn the body
with the head through X4's mouse-look).

Consequences, stated before anything is built:
* The layer must declare only the HEAD part on foot: GetCameraRotation there
  includes the body, and declaring it is what made the window swing in 334.
  Body = GetCameraRotation with our written rotation taken back out.
* Whatever else the branch covers (other states where the player object is
  the camera's parent: elevators, conversations, transporters?) gets the
  head rotation too -- probably right, to be seen.
* Picking on foot: if X4 aims the crosshair's interaction from the camera
  (as the cockpit's hover does), it follows the gaze; if from the player
  object, the highlight follows the body. The take will show which.
* +0x5b0 must be ours on foot whenever the patch is in: the head's angle, or
  identity -- never a stale cockpit angle.

## X4VR_HEADLOOK_FOOT — B built (Patola: "Yes, patch for B approved — and head alone for pitch on foot")

* **The patch** (`injector/x4vr_foot.hpp`, applied at load like
  X4VR_CSM_COVER, memory only): the walking branch's `jne 0x192a216` at
  0x192a2f3 is RETARGETED to 0x192a284 -- X4's own tail (the path modes 1
  and 6 take) that reloads the attached object's transform and composes only
  the camera's own (+0x5a0..+0x5d0). Walking renders player x head; the
  controller (the cockpit's sway chain) stays out; in the cockpit the branch
  is not taken. Four bytes (the rel32: 0xffffff1d -> 0xffffff8b); 37 bytes
  around the jne, the tail's 22 and the compose's 28 verified first, and the
  decoded targets too; read back after. Refuses without X4VR_HEADLOOK_WRITE
  (nothing would own +0x5b0 on foot). tests/foot.cpp checks the sites against
  the real binary, a one-byte change in each refused and named, the rel32.
* **Head-look on foot:** with the patch in, the write acts off the seat too

## Take 336 — SCORED FAIL: the patched branch is the COCKPIT's; on foot X4 exits earlier

Patola: *"When in the cockpit, moving the head would rotate the window in the
same direction that I turned my head ... by a bit more than I turn. And when
I leave the cockpit, headlook doesn't work, only mouse turning."* He stopped
the run there.

    seated   GetCameraRotation yaw FOLLOWS the head with slope 2.020 (43
             head-only windows; local, our write, slope 1.003)
             tracking |X4 - head| yaw median 2.47 p90 39.19 -> FAIL
             menucam: a menu period frozen at -159 deg -> FAIL
    on foot  GetCameraRotation does NOT follow the head (r 0.00, 11 windows)
             while the camera's own matrix held it (local r 0.98);
             the mouse turned the body (r -0.99, -0.12 deg/count); its pitch

    patch    IN, at load

* **P336.2 REFUTED, by exactly the refutation it named:** *"anything in the
  cockpit differs -- the walking branch would then be taken in the cockpit
  too."* It is. The retarget only changes what happens when the jne at
  0x192a2f3 is taken, and the cockpit doubled, so the cockpit takes it.
  Before the patch, then, X4 never composes the camera's own transform for
  the player's camera in the cockpit either: the free-look reaches the view
  through the PLAYER object, whose local transform (vt+0x1488 = 0x13142a0)
  is built by the first component at player+0x200 (vt+0x68) -- the seat, in
  the cockpit. Patched, the camera's own was composed on top: twice.
* **P336.3 REFUTED** on foot. Every exit of 0x1929f70 that a non-NULL
  controller can reach either composes the camera's own transform (which
  334/335 refute: our write never showed) or ends at the patched branch
  (which 336 refutes: it would have shown now). The reference (+0x788)
  cannot be NULL, or `out` would never have been evaluated and
  GetCameraRotation could not follow the mouse. **So on foot the camera's
  controller (+0x18) is NULL and X4 returns at 0x1929ffd** -- deduced, not
  yet read; the next take logs it.
* **The wrong turn, recorded:** "B, read statically" named the 0x192a2f3
  branch walking's because walking is where the write failed; it never
  established which state takes it, and the resume memory even carried
  "Unverified: controller NULL vs the branch on foot". A branch read in
  isolation was given the meaning of the symptom.
  [[hypothesis-and-fix-in-one-step]]
* **Retired:** X4VR_HEADLOOK_FOOT now refuses ("the 0x192a2f3 retarget is
  retired"), so the knob cannot double the cockpit again. The shipping line
  never carried it.

**The model now:**

    cockpit  camera = player (seat component: carries the free-look)
             -- 0x1929f70 returns at 0x192a2f3, camera's own NOT composed
    on foot  camera = player (walking component: body yaw, look pitch)
             -- 0x1929f70 returns at 0x1929ffd (controller NULL, deduced)

**B, second attempt (proposed, needs Patola's approval as its own patch):**
the controller-NULL exit at 0x1929ffd (`je 0x192a216`, 0f 84 13 02 00 00)
retargeted to a stub of ours: if this camera is the player's
(rbx == [[0x3db6948]+0x3e8]) jump to 0x192a284 -- compose the camera's own
transform, our head -- else to 0x192a216, X4's return. Scratch register r11
(unused in the function, dead after the call before it). The cockpit never
reaches it (its controller exists: 336 proves it); other cameras with no
controller return exactly as before. On foot: player (body) x head, once.
Data-only alternative: A (the body follows the head through X4's
mouse-look, gain ~0.11 deg/count measured in 335).

### The defect he flagged: on-foot submenus

*"after clicking in an interactable that has a submenu, the cursor appears
off the selected sections of the submenu, depending on where I am looking.
This is worse for submenus that are a dialog, when clicking on an NPC,
because choosing the options has less of a hover indication and that turns
the interaction very slow."*

**What the log shows.** On foot X4 freed the pointer four times with the HUD
up: 46075.4 (6.3 s), 46168.7 (17.6 s), 46195.3 (48.8 s, the long one) and
46307.4 (8.2 s). The HUD-down at 46099.8 also freed it.

* X4 reported no full-screen menu for any of them, so `X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS=auto`
  drew the cursor raw.
* Head-look kept writing throughout (HUD up). The head sat at about
  (−49°, −20°), (+7°, −21°), (+5°, −26°) and (−10°, −21°) yaw/pitch, and
  moved at most 2.4° yaw and 6° pitch within any one opening.
* On foot the head carries all the pitch (the mouse's is zeroed), so in every
  opening the head was about 20° below the body's horizon.

**Two mechanisms fit "depending on where I am looking":**

1. **The canvas (known since take 327).** This is the cockpit right-click
   menu's defect, recorded in "Take 327 — SCORED", item 4, and never fixed.
   * X4 lays its UI out scaled by the canvas map A = 0.5252 and hit-tests it
     at the raw pointer n. So the option under X4's pointer is drawn at A·n.
   * The raw cursor therefore sits 1/A ≈ 1.9 times as far from the window's
     centre as the option it selects: nothing at the centre, growing outward.
   * "Where I am looking" is then where in the window the cursor is.
2. **The head.** On foot, X4 might draw its UI through one camera and
   hit-test through another: one including head-look's part (our stub
   composes it), the other not.
   * The offset would then grow with the head's angle off the body, which on
     foot is at least the ~20° of pitch.
   * No evidence for this beyond his phrase. Recorded as the alternative to
     rule out, not reasoned away.

(1) is a measured mechanism with a known fix. (2) predicts that (1)'s fix
leaves an offset, larger the more the head is turned from the body.

## On-foot menus: the cursor through the UI canvas — built for take 339

* **`X4VR_CURSOR_CANVAS=auto` now covers on-foot menus.**
  * An opening is X4 freeing the pointer (relative mode ON→off) while
    head-look is on foot, held 50 ms. Take 338's HUD-down freed the pointer
    6 ms before X4 reported the HUD down; the HUD going down ends "on foot"
    and cancels the pending opening.
  * The stand-up arrives with the pointer already free and is no opening.
  * The state machine is `x4vr::foot::FootMenu` in `injector/x4vr_foot.hpp`,
    tested in `tests/foot.cpp`. A mutation (hold = 0) fails 6 of its 11
    cases.
  * The injector publishes `foot_menu` (share v7); the layer draws through
    the canvas while it or `fullscreen_menu` is up, and says which.
* **`X4VR_CURSOR_FOOT_AB=1`** alternates per opening: odd openings canvas
  (A), even ones raw (B, take 338's).
  * Each opening is a relayed milestone, "on-foot menu N — cursor A (canvas)",
    so he knows the arm without counting.
  * Each OPEN line logs head-look's angle and the pointer, the two quantities
    the mechanisms above disagree on.
* **Scorer `foot-menu`.** It lists every opening with its arm, duration, head
  angle, pointer and whether the canvas reached the layer. It FAILs a canvas
  opening that never reached the layer.
  * A build before this one shows only the pointer releases: "a build before
    take 339, which drew them all raw".
  * `cursor-auto` no longer counts on-foot switches as full-screen ones.
  * Planted cases: tests/run-census-scorer.sh, with a guard on the injector's
    and the layer's format strings.
* **Read-back skipped on foot**, see above. The cockpit is unchanged.

## Built for take 341: the vendor's Cancel; canvas under the centring by default

* **FootMenu resumes a menu the HUD interrupted.** A menu that was open when
  the HUD went down opens again (held 50 ms) when the HUD comes back up with
  the pointer free. It is logged "(still free after a HUD-down menu)".
* **Replayed through the real FootMenu** (`step` driven by takes 338–340's
  relative/HUD/seat events at 10 ms):
  * 340 gains exactly one opening, at 54131.27: the vendor after Cancel,
    50 ms after the HUD came up.
  * 339 gains one false one, at 50996.84. There the map was opened FROM an
    on-foot menu that X4 does not bring back, and the pointer stayed free
    0.9 s before X4 took it. Recorded in the code as the known false case:
    a soon-hidden cursor drawn at the canvas scale for 0.9 s.
  * An earlier version (any free pointer on foot, once X4 had held it)
    would also have fired after a map opened while walking. The test
    covers it.
* **Canvas under the menu centring is the behaviour**: the next line drops
  X4VR_CURSOR_CENTRED_AB. A won where it was tested.
* Scorer: `hud-menu` reads the canvas state over time and names the
  full-screen periods; `foot-menu` marks resumed openings. Planted cases for
  both; take 340's false FAIL is a case.

* **The pointer to the window's centre on a fresh on-foot opening**
  (Patola, on the second question: *"Yes, I definitely want the cursor closer
  to the menus"*).
  * On by default; `X4VR_FOOT_MENU_RECENTRE=0` leaves it where X4 freed it.
  * Through the same warp as the steering recentre: `recentre_pointer`,
    split out of `steer_recentre`, whose log lines are unchanged.
  * Not on a resumed opening: there the pointer is where he last saw and
    moved it.
  * The scorer counts recentres against fresh openings.

**Protected UI Mode, answered (his first question, before deciding):**
* **The shadow fix is not an extension.** It is the injector's code patch
  (X4VR_CSM_COVER, csmfit).
* **Our three extensions are XML diffs of `libraries/parameters.xml`**
  (look-around limits, sway off, the head-look follower). There is no Lua,
  so Protected UI Mode does not touch them.
* **Neither his `config.xml` nor our fork sets `uisafemode`**, so X4's
  default is in force.
* **What it restricts**, per X4's binary: `require()` takes only
  whitelisted modules, and native libraries must be signed. X4's own text
  for the option: protects the system "against malicious actions by third
  party modifications".
* **Off would apply to the mod's sessions only**, through our config fork.
  It would lift that protection for every enabled UI mod in those sessions,
  not just ours: he has one Workshop extension enabled (ws_1666869624).
* **An alternative that needs no setting**: the injector, already native
  code in X4's process, asks X4's own menu Lua state whether the interact
  menu is open, each tick, between X4's Lua calls.
  * X4's interact menu source is readable (`menu_interactmenu.lua`).
  * Riskier to build (the right `lua_State`, the right moment on X4's
    thread), but nothing is lowered and nothing installed.

## Built for take 342: dialogue start from X4's conversation state; X4's open-menu table read

* **IsConversationActive is read, not called** (`injector/x4vr_menus.hpp`).
  * Declared in ego_detailmonitorhelper/helper.lua as
    `bool IsConversationActive(void)`.
  * At 0xc02dc0 it is `*(int *)(*(void **)0x3db8300 + 0x1a0) != 1` with no
    NULL check on the global, so the injector reads those bytes through
    self_read instead.
  * On a fresh on-foot opening the pointer goes to x centre, y 2070/2816
    during a conversation, else to the centre. The log says which.
* **X4's table of open menus, read: the no-setting route for the cockpit
  right-click menu.**
  * IsFullscreenMenuDisplayed (already polled) looks a menu up by name in a
    tree rooted at 0x3dfc208 and returns the found node's full-screen flag.
    Lua's right-click menu is "InteractMenu", not full-screen, so asking the
    function says nothing about it.
  * Node layout, from the lookup (0xbb0860..) and the in-order walk at
    0x117f7c0: left child +0x08, right +0x10, the name's std::string at
    +0x20/+0x28, the flag at +0x40. It is not libstdc++'s map layout.
  * The injector walks it at 10 Hz on X4's main thread, bounded at 64 nodes;
    a cycle, a failed read or a non-text name refuses the walk. It logs every
    change of the set: "ui: X4's open menus: InteractMenu, MapMenu[full]".
  * Sites: 5 instruction runs (85 bytes) plus both RIP targets, checked
    against the real binary in tests/menus.cpp; a one-byte flip at either
    end of each is refused and named. 17 cases, including the walk's
    refusals on fakes laid out as the disassembly says.
* **Scorer:** `menus` lists every change with seat/foot and the names seen,
  and says whether InteractMenu was ever in the table. `foot-menu` counts
  recentres by kind. Planted cases with format guards.

## Take 345 — the volumetric nebula differs between the eyes

Patola: in Matrix #79B (dumps n16–n23) *"a background nebula is shifted by
at least 60° in one of the eyes compared to the other"*; in CEO's Doubt
(n33–n41), from inside a station and from the external view, *"a nebula
that's shifted / occupying different parts of the sky"*.

**What the dumps show** (`/tmp/x4vr-t345-present-nNN-layer{0,1}.png`, the
eye images as submitted):
* **Only the nebula differs.** The cockpit, the station, ships, stars and
  the sun agree between the eyes. In Matrix #79B the left eye has a bright
  cloud across the middle of the sky; the right eye has it displaced left,
  mostly out of view. In CEO's Doubt the green fog's dark gap sits in a
  different place in each eye.
* **Not head-look.** n36/n37 are the external view, where head-look does
  not act (X4's camera reads 0,0), and they split the same way.
* **Not every nebula.** n12, a grey nebula in another sector, agrees
  between the eyes.

**What draws it.** These two sectors have X4's volumetric fog:
`volume_raymarch3.frag.glsl` with `volume_*.comp`, `volume_apply`,
`volume_blend` (`p1_sector_fog`, `p1_fog_volume`).
* The ray march builds its ray as
  `Ray(V_cameraposition, view2world_rot(UnProjectUJ(clip)))`, that is
  `M_viewinverse · M_invproj_uj`, and intersects a box of
  `U_volume_box_position`/`U_volume_box_dimensions` in sector space,
  thousands of metres across.
* **The hypothesis, not yet measured:** in the right eye this pass reads
  the wrong camera data, through the per-eye index offset or the mirrored
  camera block.
  * A wrong camera POSITION would show the sector-space box from somewhere
    else, while camera-relative geometry stays right. That is the pattern
    in the dumps.
  * A wrong rotation would do it too. Which one is the next question.

## Take 346 — SCORED FAIL (after the fix below): the shader dumps were never written

Patola teleported to Matrix #79B and looked at the nebula for well over 30 s,
including the external and target views.

**The dumps did not happen, and the run scored PASS.**
* The layer opens `$X4VR_DUMP_SHADERS/mod-NNNN.spv` and does not create the
  directory. `/tmp/x4vr-shaders` did not exist, so it warned once and wrote
  nothing. I had not checked that precondition before the hand-off, and the
  scorer did not look.
* **A second defect behind it:** the warning appeared twice because gamescope
  loads the layer as well (inert there) and dumped its own modules. Its
  serials start at 0 like X4's, so with the directory present the two
  processes would have overwritten each other's `mod-NNNN.spv`.
* **Fixed:**
  * only the game dumps;
  * the layer makes the directory;
  * a `modules: dumping` line says it is writing.
  * Proven through the layer on a real GPU (tests/multiview_render, app
    "X4"): the missing directory was created and 3 modules written.
  * The scorer FAILs a run that asked and wrote none (planted cases). Take
    346 now scores FAIL.

**What the run still gives, from the pipeline and render-pass inventories:**
* Five full-screen pipelines were first built after the arrival (the map
  closed at 101692.7):
  * four drawn once (`MONO`, `original`) in their own passes: #40, #71 (two)
    and #73;
  * one in the main scene pass #33, which the mod patched for the second eye.
* Passes #71 and #73 are `1 colour [97H] (R16G16B16A16) → MONO (fullscreen
  post) +MASKED(fullscreen)`, i.e. drawn into both layers.
* Some fragment modules in #40 sample the bindless table with
  `index-offset APPLIED`, so in view 1 they read the layer-1 twin of a
  doubled image.
* That is the shape of a volumetric pipeline (ray march into its own target,
  then composite). Which module is the fog's ray march needs the dumps.
